The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed technique are validated by the results of the corresponding numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Delay and Phase Prediction Method for Distributed Coherence-synthesizing Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Distributed Coherence-synthesizing Radar efficiently use multi-radar airspace and energy resources to significantly improve radar detection range and measurement accuracy, providing a solution to the contradiction between long range detect and flexibility. However, for high-speed targets, the fast movement leads to parameters estimation for Coherence-synthesizing lagging behind actual target's location. Under these circumstance parameters estimation must be predicted in order to achieve Transmit-Receive-Coherence. This passage firstly builds the signal model of parameters estimation for Distributed Coherence-synthetic Radar and gives the variation pattern of parameters caused by target motion, then proposes a new prediction method of delay and phase for Coherence-synthetic based on the tracking filter model. At last, actual radar tracking data will be analyzed, whose result verify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Detection Performance of Passive Bistatic Radar Based on NCAF
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Cross ambiguity processing is commonly used for target detection in passive bistatic radar systems. Analytical expression is obtained for the probability density function (PDF) of normalized cross ambiguity function (NCAF) when the data samples in the target surveillance and reference channels are contaminated by narrowband uncorrelated white Gaussian noises. The cumulative distribution function (CDF) for NCAF is then derived, and applied to detect which cell in the ambiguity surface exceeds a preset threshold, which determined by a given false-alarm probability. Results are presented in the form of curves showing the values of input SNRs required to achieve a specified detection probability for various combinations of signal's parameters.

articleTitle: Construction of Large Scale Flexible Load Resource Control System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: “Flexible load” refers to the load whose power consumption varies within a specified interval or transfers between different periods, including adjustable or transferable loads with demand elasticity. Establishing a flexible load resource control platform can carry out consultative and planned load dissipation according to the actual supply and demand situation and regulation ability of industrial and commercial users, while ensuring that their rigid power demand is not affected by load dissipation, supplemented by economic compensation measures, to encourage industrial and commercial users to actively cooperate with regulation and control. In this paper, a new large-scale flexible load participating in power grid regulation system is proposed. Real-time acquisition of user parameters is realized through platform software, control terminals, and auxiliary metering instruments. Coordination operation of power grid source-network-load is realized through large-scale flexible load participating in power grid regulation based on data-driven, which helps users save energy and increase efficiency.

articleTitle: Object Recognition of Three-dimensional SAR Based on PointNet
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Object recognition of three-dimensional (3-D) SAR is one of the hot areas in the SAR application field. In order to improve the performance of 3-D SAR target recognition, this paper proposes a novel deep learning method for 3-D point-cloud recognition based on PointNet classification network. In the scheme, a point cloud extraction model is used to 3-D SAR image, then a PointNet network is trained with the extracted point cloud data. The effectiveness of the approach is verified by 3-D SAR simulation images with three different airplane targets. The results demonstrate that the method can obtain a high recognition accuracy in the case of a low 3-D SAR resolution.

articleTitle: Post Compensation of Weak Nonlinearity for Digital Receiver
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a calibration algorithm for weak nonlinear system based on a Hammerstein model. The differences of self-correlation performance are utilized for the separation of strong signals which would cause nonlinear distortion. The strong signals are also employed as the objective reference signal for blindidentification and adaptive updating of Hammerstein model coefficients. In the process of system identification, the input signal is unknown and can be hardly obtained. However, this long-standing problem can be solved by the separation algorithm proposed in this paper. The blind identification algorithm of nonlinear model is applied for the digital calibration of weak nonlinear circuit. The experimental results on actual circuit indicate that the spurs-free dynamic range can be improved by 10 dB.The design of high-precision, high-speed software defined system could benefit much from this novel technical solution.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation for Hyperspectral Target Detection with Adaptive Coherence Estimator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) offer promising tools for real-time on-board hyperspectral image (HSI) processing due to its higher computational speed and better reconfigurability. In this paper, the spectral matching target detection algorithm, namely adaptive coherence estimator (ACE), is implemented based on FPGA. The flow background statistics are used to calculate the background covariance matrix, and the Sherman-Morrison method is further used to process the covariance matrix inversion. The finally calculated results should separate targets from the whole pixels by a selected threshold. Evaluation of several hyperspectral data shows that the system has a higher speed than the traditional 3.60GHz CPU (about 77.74 times) without losing accuracy.

articleTitle: Multiple Object Localization and Vital Sign Monitoring Using a MIMO IR-UWB Radar System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We develop a prototype 2×2 multi-input multi-output (MIMO) impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) radar system to simultaneously localize multiple objects and monitor their vital signs. We first provide a brief description of the hardware prototype system. We then use a modified back projection (BP) algorithm to localize multiple human objects. Next, an iterative adaptive approach (IAA) is applied to estimate their vital sign parameters. Finally, the implementation of the experiments using the MIMO hardware system is described and the measured results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Wigner distribution in linear canonical domains: properties and discretization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In our previous work, we introduced a kind of closed-form linear canonical transform (LCT) based Wigner distribution (WD), namely, the closed-form instantaneous cross-correlation function type of WD (CICFWD), and discussed its applications in non-stationary signal separation and detection. However, some related theoretical foundations are still unknown. The purpose of this paper is to revisit the CICFWD by establishing its essential theories including main properties and discretization for the requirement of practical applications.

articleTitle: Simulation of Phase Characteristics of Underwater Target Acoustic Scattering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Acoustic scattering phase of underwater target is one of the key scattering characteristics, which can be used as an extra parameter for target detection and an identifier for target identification. On the basis of analyzing and processing the simulation data of benchmark scaled model, the phase characteristics of acoustic scattering signals associated with the attribute information of underwater target are proposed and researched. The law of the phase characteristics with frequency and target azimuth are obtained. It shows that the research on the phase of target acoustic scattering can increase the amount of information which can be utilized in target detection and recognition. The results demonstrate that the target phase characteristics will be important for the acquisition of increased levels of information, critical for the development of automated targets detection and species identification.

articleTitle: The Joint Detector Based On Prior Knowledge for Multipath Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This work deduces a novel joint detector taking advantage of multipath signal with the prior knowledge of multipath environment, which has a better detection performance than the conventional one. The available specular reflection is mainly considered and modeled as the prior knowledge of multipath environment. Subsequently, a Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) is used to explore the novel joint detector combining Line Of Sight (LOS) and multipath signal. Numerical simulation results show that utilizing multipath signal could improve radar detection performance evidently when the multipath amplitude exceeds three-fifty of the LOS signal.

articleTitle: Tensor Based Analysis Dictionary Learning for Color Video Denoising
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, by utilizing the tensor computation, we propose a novel analysis dictionary learning (ADL) algorithm named tensor analysis dictionary learning (TADL) to effectively represent multidimensional (MD) signals and apply it for color video (four-dimensional signal) denoising. By incorporating correlations among various channels, TADL can handle an arbitrary order tensor of the MD signals more naturally. Different from what is performed in existing ADL algorithms, in TADL the dimensional features of the MD signals are represented by a series of dictionaries collaboratively, and the dictionary atoms are updated simultaneously by adopting the simultaneous codeword optimization (SimCO) on tensors, leading to a computationally efficient optimization process. Experiments show that, 1) the proposed TADL algorithm can deal with color video denoising well, which is impossible for the standard ADL algorithm, and 2) when the noise intensity is relatively high, TADL outperforms state-of-the-art ADL algorithms in terms of computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Waveforms for Joint Wireless Communication and High Resolution SAR Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Special attention has been devoted to joint wireless communication and radar sensing systems in recent years. However, since communication and radar have conflict requirements in terms of transceiver developments and signal processing algorithms, specifically of the waveforms, this joint concept realization is still a great challenge. In this paper, we mainly focus on the waveform schemes. From the viewpoint of the energy conservation law, the conventional joint waveform drawbacks are analyzed, and the multidimensional waveforms are proposed. Following which, the space time coding (STC) waveform scheme, along with a C band MIMO system, are designed for the realization of joint wireless communication and SAR imaging. Theoretical analysis is validated by laboratory and flight experiments. It can be concluded from the experimental results that, by employing the multidimensional waveform, we can perform both data transmission and high-resolution SAR imaging at the same time without intra-modal interference. Through our analysis, we aim to open up a new perspective of using multidimensional waveform to realize joint communication and radar systems.

articleTitle: A Three-Dimensional Imaging Method Based on Peak Detection for Multi-angle SAR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has been widely used in military reconnaissance, civil construction and scientific research because of its day and night, all-weather, and global observation capabilities. In order to reconstruct the third dimension of targets, a spaceborne multi-angle SAR system has been proposed. In this paper, a novel imaging method based on peak detection is proposed for multi-angle SAR system. The height error can affect the quality of the focused SAR images. The height of target can be obtained by searching the maximum position of the focused pixel. The effectiveness of the method is validated by simulated data.

articleTitle: A Dimensional Reduction Visualization Method for Large Data of Power Grid Based on t-SNE Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The large data of power grid includes the data generated or needed in the process of planning, operation, management, and operation of distribution power system, including power generation data, transmission data, distribution data, power consumption data, and external data (such as economic, social and meteorological data). Data dimension is high and visualization is difficult. In this paper, a dimensionality reduction visualization method based on the t-SNE algorithm for large data of power grid is proposed. The dimensionality reduction of large data of high-dimensional power grid is processed on the premise of maintaining local geometric characteristics. Because the t-SNE algorithm has the ability to process non-linear and high-dimensional data, it can meet the needs of multi-type data fusion analysis and processing in a smart grid. In this paper, the 96-dimensional load data in the Shanghai area is used for visualization simulation, and good results are obtained, which provides a novel slotion for the visualization of large data in the high-dimensional power grid.

articleTitle: A high-precision position finding method for short baseline radar system
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a high-precision position finding method for short baseline radar system based on phase-derived range and angle measurement. Multiple baselines are utilized to measure the azimuth and elevation angle based on phased-derived angle measurement method, while the target range is measured based on phased-derived range measurement. The phase-derived range and angle measurement has much higher accuracy than envelope-based methods, thus can achieve high-precision position finding. The performance of the proposed method is verified by simulation and ejection ball experiment.

articleTitle: Fuzzy ARTMAP Network And Clustering For Streaming Classification Under Emerging New Classes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Streaming classification with emerging new classes is a challenging problem receiving extensive attention. To date, most approaches simply detect novel classes without further recognizing them, and ignore conceptual drift and conceptual evolution problem. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an effective semi-supervised framework that combines ARTMAP neural network and clustering method to detect and identify simultaneously multiple known and unknown classes in data streams and update the network online. Experiments have been conducted on four benchmark datasets with different data forms including MNIST, CIFAR10, network attack analysis, and geospatial information of forests. The empirical evaluation shows effectiveness of the proposed approach, whose results are much better than many previous studies.

articleTitle: Fast Digital Beamforming for Conformal Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The conventional digital beam forming (DBF) for conformal array needs to scan a series of look angles with small angular separation to obtain a high-resolution pattern. Inspired by the fast back projection algorithm (FBP)[3] for SAR imaging, a fast DBF algorithm for the conformal array is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the conformal array is divided into several subarrays, and the pattern of each subarray is formed in a coarse resolution. Then, the pattern of each subarray is interpolated to a high resolution one by FFT. Finally, all subarrays' high-resolution pattern is added together to form the pattern of the whole array. The simulation results have proved the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Classification and Identification of Micro-Doppler Signatures of Pedestrian and Cyclists Using Simulated Data and ELM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: There are great interests to study detection, and classification of pedestrian and cyclists using low-cost frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar sensors for intelligent transport systems (ITS). This paper presents a study about detection and classification of pedestrian and/or cyclists based on realistically simulated FMCW radar sensor echoes. From radar echoes, the micro-Doppler signatures of different targets can be observed through time-velocity diagrams and then extracted. Using a relatively small number of data samples for training, an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) can be trained to detect the number of targets and classify their types. Numerical experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach and the potential of low-cost radar sensors in ITS applications.

articleTitle: A method of underwater target detection via nonnegative matrix factorization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Reverberation is the unavoidable interference for an active sonar. It makes difficult to detect an underwater target. The theory of low-rank and sparse matrix decomposition provides a new idea for underwater target detection. Inspired by this theory, we propose a method via non-negative matrix factorization (NMF). The method first extracts the low-rank structure and then separates targets from reverberation through iterations. Simulation is performed to verify its feasibility and to evaluate with the ROC curve.

articleTitle: The FPGA Implementation of Low-Altitude and Slow-Speed Small Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, there are more and more low-altitude slow-speed aircrafts, like unmanned rotorcraft and powered parachute. Whether in the military or civilian fields, it is necessary to detect and track these targets. Hardware implementation of a low-altitude and slow-speed small (LSS) target detection method is presented in this paper. The spectrum zoom processing method is the core of this algorithm. There are many devices available to accomplish the LSS target detection algorithm, like GPU, DSP. In consideration of the fixed and repetitive operations at high data rate in this algorithm, the FPGA implementation scheme is a better choice to construct the processing system. We implement the LSS target detection in FPGA. The spectrum zoom processing operation is implemented by parallel group of FFT magnitude calculation modules, and the system is built on a processing board whose core is the XV7K325T chip.

articleTitle: Spaceborne Bistatic InSAR Geolocation with Geostationary Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The bistatic interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) system, with a geosynchronous earth orbit (GEO) illuminator and two low-earth-orbit (LEO) receivers, has the advantages of flexibility, lightweight receiving platform and low cost. However, its geometry of bistatic interferometry is complex, and its slant range equation is in the form of round-trip delay. The traditional three-dimensional (3D) positioning methods of InSAR with `one-transmitter and two-receivers' and repeat tracks are invalid. In order to solve this problem, firstly, we establish the bistatic InSAR target positioning equations. Secondly, according to the interferometric geometry, the conversion relationship between baseline vector and slant range vector is constructed. Then, we derive and present a closed-form solution of the bistatic InSAR target positioning in the form of geostationary GEO SAR orbit. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation data.

articleTitle: Signal Detection Based on Recursive Autocorrelation and mn Method for Synchronous Nyquist Folding Receiver
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Synchronous Nyquist folding receiver (SNYFR) is an improved novel broadband receiver architecture that is possible to implement in the engineering. The output signal of SNYFR is usually a hybrid modulated signal, so corresponding signal detection methods need to be investigated, which is the premise of precise parameter estimation. In this paper, a signal detection method based on recursive autocorrelation and mn method for SNYFR is proposed. First, autocorrelation with a fixed length for SNYFR output signal is acquired. Then, in order to determine the existence of the signal, constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detector is introduced into the method to generate an adaptive threshold. Finally, the position where the signal exists is determined by mn method and the signal data are sent to back-end processor for parameter estimation. The proposed algorithm can not only adapt to low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), but also has a high measurement accuracy with low computational complexity. The simulation demonstrates the viability and validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of M-ary and CSK Spread Spectrum Communication over Deep-sea Vertical Channel
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper is concerned with two classical modulation schemes of M-ary and CSK in spread spectrum technology, our treatment is focused on the communication performance of two schemes in the deep-sea vertical channel. We process long-term experimental data with sea-depth from 1207m to 3870m for three times, and present the deep-sea vertical channel properties such as the time-delay spread, the amplitude of the successive paths and the time-varying multipath structure. The influence of the deep-sea vertical channel on the communication performance of the two schemes is analyzed, their performance are compared based on the experimental data.

articleTitle: Classification of Pedestrian Motion Based on Micro-Doppler Feature with LFMCW RADAR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The use of millimeter-wave radar has become a focus recently thanks to the reduced cost. One of the important applications of millimeter-wave radar is pedestrian behavior testing. The micro-Doppler feature of human can effectively realize pedestrian behavior monitoring. Mobile phones bring convenience to people and bring danger. Using mobile phone while walking can cause people to be absent-minded. This paper presents a detection method based on radar micro-Doppler feature analysis for pedestrians using mobile phones. By studying and comparing the micro-Doppler information of pedestrian activities using mobile phones, special features are extracted and used to detect dangerous behaviors. The method was validated using the 77GHz LFMCW radar.

articleTitle: Full-time Resolution analysis and Path Determination for air borne Forward-Looking SAR with Opportunistic Illuminator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The bistatic SAR has forward-looking imaging capabilities if a opportunistic illuminator is selected to form the synthetic aperture. This would enable it to perform some inspection tasks that traditional SAR cannot perform. The system resolution of a bistatic SAR is related to its configuration. Due to the special configuration of the bistatic forward-looking SAR, the traditional system trajectory design method is no longer applicable. Therefore, a trajectory design method used for bistatic forward-looking SAR is proposed in this paper. First, the original trajectory of the receiver is determined according to the system which is always cannot be changed. Then, the slant range and the pitch angle of the transmitter are determined at each time. Next, the resolution of the transmitter under different squint angles at different times is calculated. Then, the available area of squint angle is obtained by drawing the results into a diagram. Finally, a position curve of the squint angle that is contained within the available area is found, and then the position of the transmitter and the resolution are calculated based on the position curve. The method can make the resolution of the forward-looking SAR system meet the requirements at all times under the condition that the changes to the original trajectory are at the minimum. The simulation results verify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Word length Optimization Method for Radix-2k Fixed-Point Pipeline FFT Processors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to overcome the disadvantages of higher logic resource occupancy when implementing a radix-2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup> fixed-point pipelined FFT processor with single-path delay feedback architecture, the word length optimization method is proposed. Under the premise of the output signal quantization noise ratio (SQNR) which needs to be achieved, the optimized word length required for each butterfly operation stage can be obtained by direct formula calculation based on theoretical derivation and mathematical modeling, providing the theoretical basis for the word length configuration for the implementation of the fixed-point pipelined FFT processor. Compared with some previous works, the fixed-point pipeline FFT processor realized with the proposed method has the advantages of lower storage resource occupation while ensuring the processing precision.

articleTitle: Critical and Optimal Baseline Of Single-Pass Single-Antenna Squint Angle Airborne InSAR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Single-pass single-antenna interferometric synthetic aperture radar (SS-InSAR), in the configuration of single-pass and single-antenna with squint angles, has already shown its simplicity in retrieving digital terrain models. In this paper, the elevation uncertainty is derived and the error sources are analysed for SS-InSAR. Under the guidance of height uncertainty and decorrelation of SS-InSAR, the critical baseline is derived and the optimal baseline is presented. Finally, the computer simulation results of the measurement accuracy as well as the critical and optimal baseline is given, which can guide the baseline design of the SS-InSAR system.

articleTitle: A Low-PAPR Underwater Acoustic Multiuser Communication Algorithm Based on Selective Differential Coding and SC-FDMA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Underwater acoustic communication transmission consumes relatively high power, so the system needs to have a lower Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR). In this paper, a low-PAPR underwater acoustic multiuser communication algorithm based on Selective Differential Coding and Single-carrier Frequency Division Multiple Access (SLD-SC-FDMA) was proposed in allusion to the PAPR problem in underwater acoustic Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) system. At the transmitting end, the signal is differentially coded into a baseband symbol by multiple sets of initial phases; Discrete Fourier Transform is performed for the target user's frequency band, and the information of each baseband symbol is distributed to all frequency bands of the user, then the sum of information on all frequencies at each moment is a baseband symbol; the actual symbol information in the space (when the symbol is simultaneously transmitted in the full frequency domain) is calculated with Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform for all frequencies; and the group that minimizes PAPR is selected and added with a cyclic prefix before being sent out through the transducer. At the receiving end, the demodulation process opposite to the transmitting end is completed, and the original bit information is estimated. Good simulation and experimental results verified the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A-KNN: An adaptive method for constructing high-resolution ocean models
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Given the low resolution of ocean data, this paper proposes a method to construct a high-resolution ocean data model, adaptively selecting the optimal parameters for the model. The KNN regression model proposed in this paper is used to refine the seawater thermocline data, which significantly improves the data resolution on the vertical gradient. The proposed method is an improvement on the KNN regression model so that the model can adaptively select parameters based on the input data. The trained model can predict the temperature and salinity data at any position in the experimental area, and solve the low resolution caused by the sparse deployment of underwater nodes. The simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively select the optimal parameters for the KNN model.

articleTitle: A Conical Helix Array For Small Autonomous Underwater Platforms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the large diameters and high power consumption, the traditional arrays are difficult to be equipped on small autonomous underwater platforms. A conical helix array with small apertures is designed for the installation on the head of the autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV), which aims at the localization of underwater acoustic source. The design principle of the conical helix array is based on the completeness of the spherical harmonic functions. The conical helix array has 16 hydrophones, evenly distributed on two spiral curves. The localization of the acoustic source is realized by applying the spherical harmonics domain matching field processing. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed conical helix array can effectively achieve three-dimensional localization of the point source in the waveguide.

articleTitle: Unimodular Phase-coded Waveforms with Low Sidelobes over Desired Range-Doppler Regions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a unimodular phase-coded waveform design method for suppressing range-Doppler sidelobes over desired regions of the ambiguity function (AF) is proposed using the adaptive moment estimation (ADAM) algorithm. Simulations show that desired regional range-Doppler sidelobes in the AF can be flexibly and effectively suppressed.

articleTitle: An experimental demonstration of detection of acoustic aberration caused by submerged intruder in littoral water based on WRELAX - NRTR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The strong “direct blast” and space-time varying environment lead to significant difficulty in the detection of the submerged target that makes acoustic aberrations occur due to forward scattering. An improved acoustic aberration detection method called WRELAX-NRTR is provided which combining the nonreciprocal time reversal with a high-resolution channel estimation technique WRELAX. An experiment with a diver target conducted in the shallow littoral environment would verify that the proposed algorithm could efficiently achieve the target detection with higher detection probability.

articleTitle: Logarithmic Texture Analysis for Early Lung Cancer Screening on Contrast Enhancement CT Images
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the effects of contrast enhancement computed tomography (CECT) images on the malignant distinguishes of solid lung nodules. As a representational describer of tumor heterogeneity on images, texture features are used as the classification basis for lung cancers and non-cancers in this preliminary study. 49 patients with malignant bias suspicious lung nodules (all about 3cm) underwent non-contrast and contrast enhancement CT in arterial and venous phases were collected. And the biopsy reports show that there are 28 malignant (or cancer) and 21 benign (or non-cancer) nodules. To enlarge the feature difference between malignant and benign nodules, we proposed an improved logarithmic texture feature analysis scheme. Support vector machine classification and leave-one-out validation were implemented. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves of the non-contrast and contrast enhancement CT images in arterial and venous phases are 0.67, 0.73 and 0.77 respectively. Therefore the texture features presented by contrast enhancement CT images show better distinguishing capacity on solid lung nodules than the non-contrast enhancement CT images.

articleTitle: Direction Finding With Partially Corrupted Data Based on OptSpace Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: It is known that, if a low-rank matrix has partial entries in random locations being missing, the matrix completion technique can be used to restore the matrix. However, when the missing elements are distributed in an entire row or column, there is no enough information to directly recover the data. This paper considers such a problem: in the data matrix of a sensor array system for direction finding, the entries in an entire row (possibly several rows) are corrupted or missing, due to, for example, down-sampling or some of the array elements are damaged or turned off. To tackle this problem, we propose to utilize the spatial smoothing scheme to construct an extended data matrix which allows us to apply the matrix completion technique. Then, a gradient descent algorithm, namely OptSpace, is adopted to solve the resulting matrix completion problem. By doing so, the restored data matrix can be obtained, and the autocorrelation matrix can be computed. Finally, the directions of arrival (DOAs) are estimated with the traditional MUSIC algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Context Complexity Metric of Association Problem for Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Association is a key problem in multi-target tracking whose performance is highly affected by the context. However, how to define the context complexity of the association problem in different scenarios is rarely studied in literatures. In this paper, separation degree of association which is derived from Jensen-Shannon divergence is defined to measure this complexity in target association problem. The expression of separation degree of association is used in two examples, which shows that the difficulty of association is affected by the measurement error, detection frequency, observation geometry and the maneuvering of target.

articleTitle: A Physical Layer Key Generation method with Reliable Negotiation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: There is a risk of information leakage in the process of wireless communication. The introduction of key generation in the physical layer can effectively improve the security of wireless communication. This paper proposes a new physical layer key generation method in the TDD (time division duplex) communication system. Assume that the uplink and downlink channels are reciprocal. Through LDPC (Low Density Parity Check)channel coding and negotiation algorithm, the inconsistency rate of key generation between Alice and Bob is reduced. Simulation and analysis results show that the method improves the key generation rate and reduces the key inconsistency rate.

articleTitle: Multi-format speech perception hashing algorithm based on frequency band variance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of single speech format, no universal algorithm, low efficiency, low accuracy of tamper detection and location in small-scale of existing speech content authentication algorithms, a multi-format speech perception hashing algorithm based on frequency band variance is proposed. Firstly, the speech signal is preprocessed, framed and windowed, and the frequency band variance of each frame is calculated. Then, the hash sequence is constructed by difference hashing. Finally, the overvall security of the algorithm is improved by using logistic chaotic map to scramble and encrypt the hash of equal length. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm not only has good efficiency, key dependence, robustness and discrimination, but also has a good compromise between robustness and discrimination.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Three-Dimentional Imaging Using Single-Pass Multi-Azimuth-Angle SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of three-dimensional (3-D) image obtained by processing single-pass multi-azimuth-angle (SP-MAA) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data is analyzed and the result shows that it is unsuitable for 3-D imaging using SP-MAA SAR data. Firstly, the imaging geometry and signal model of the SP-MAA SAR are built. Then, the 3-D imaging algorithm is used to process the SP-MAA SAR data, and the 3-D image is obtained. Thirdly, the performance of the 3-D image is analyzed, and there are many ghost targets caused by azimuth sidelobes of the true targets in the 3-D image, which means it is unsuitable to obtain 3-D image using the SP-MAA SAR data. Finally, the simulation results verify the analysis results.

articleTitle: A FPGA-based Implementation of V-BLAST MIMO-OFDM Communication System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we design a V-BLAST MIMO-OFDM communication system with high capacity and high spectrum utilization rate. We exploit a non-feedback pipelined architecture for a 2×2 V-BLAST MIMO-OFDM and implement our system only by Analogs AD9361 RF Agile Transceiver and Xilinxs ZC706 FPGA development kits, which makes our system more compact and efficient. The experiment results illustrates a 150Mbps data transmission with 64QAM and 40MHz bandwidth by using our system.

articleTitle: Method for generating infrared big data for deep learning algorithm training by using small sample data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With regard to precision guided weapon, a large amount of feature data is required for the training of non-cooperative target deep learning recognition models. In this paper, based on the remote sensing data and target temperature information, the variable parameters of big data generation are proposed by analyzing the formation mechanism of infrared radiation characteristics. And then, the 3D temperature field of the target is constructed based on small sample information. Finally, based on the 3D temperature field, multiple sets of infrared characteristic data are generated with different observation angles and sun positions. By analyzing the data results, it can be seen that when the observation angle is changed, the variation of the tank barrel radiation characteristics are up to 80%, and when the position of the sun is changed, the variation of the tank hatch radiation characteristics is up to 100%. The big data generation method proposed in this paper has the characteristics of diverse characteristics, high data scalability and high feature continuity, and can be used as training data for deep learning models.

articleTitle: Research on the adjacency effect for off-nadir optical remote sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the application of the multi-angle remote sensing which obtain earth's surface data through several scan angles, the analysis of the adjacency effect in off-nadir optical remote sensing is significant. Monte Carlo method is used to simulate the atmospheric point spread function (PSF) that are appropriate for the off-nadir optical remote sensing. By the convolution of the atmospheric PSF and the surface-leaving radiance, the radiance caused by the adjacency effect could be calculated. The influence factor analysis shows that, in addition to the surface albedo and the meteorological range, the viewing direction will affect the adjacency effect dramatically. With the deviation of the viewing zenith angle from the nadir, adjacency effect becomes weak. Unlike the nadir remote sensing, the adjacency effect in off-nadir remote sensing is azimuthally dependent and the contribution of the background in the viewing direction is greater than others. Based on a three-dimensional scene and a whole chain optical imaging simulation software, the images before the optical system of the sensor with and without the adjacency effect are simulated. The calculation of the SNR, contrast and spatial resolution of the images reveals that the adjacency effect seriously degrades the image quality. These results could provide the basis for modeling the multi-angle optical remote sensing imaging system and exploring the correction algorithm of the adjacency effect.

articleTitle: Multiple-PRF Set Selection based on Skyline Diagram
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In multiple pulse repetition frequencies (PRFs) radars, the PRF set is used to resolve the ambiguities in both range and Doppler frequency. In this paper, a novel PRF selection scheme is proposed. The optimization is driven by the requirement to maximize the decodable velocity space for low PRF applications. Considering the influence of the measurement errors on the velocity decodability, the velocity skyline diagram which is termed the decodability margin is concerned during the optimization process by the genetic algorithm (GA). Simulation experiments are presented to validate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed algorithm in finding a optimal PRF set.

articleTitle: An Image Registration Algorithm Based on Slope and Distance Ratio Constraints
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of long time and low accuracy in scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) image registration, an improved SIFT image registration method based on slope and distance ratio constraints is proposed in this paper. First, the images are registration with SIFT algorithm, and a special type of error match elimination method is given. Then the matching results are screened according to the matching slope, and finally the matching results are purified by the constraint of distance ratio. Experiment results show that the method has good robustness and can reduce the time of matching process effectively in different images.

articleTitle: AdaBoostNet: An Efficient Hierarchical Neural Network for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Hierarchical Neural Networks [e.g., deep neural networks (DNNs)] have recently gained increasing attention for image classification task. Most of the previous works devote to stack multiple levels of feature learning modules with the hope that higher level modules can represent more abstract semantics of the image data. However, training of such hierarchical network is typically cast as a time-consuming non-convex optimization problem, and its effectiveness for image feature representation critically depends on expertise in parameter tuning with various ad hoc tricks. To address these issues, we advocate a biologically-inspired hierarchical neural network. One key philosophy is that the higher-level modules in the network should correct misclassification induced by the lower ones. Given this idea, a sequential stacking strategy of basic feature learning modules is presented. In practical, an efficient layer wise learning and decision aggregation method is applied to boost the hierarchical network, which is different from naive layers cascading and end-to-end finetuning, and we term it as AdaboostNet. Moreover, the basic feature learning module is set as extreme learning machine (ELM), an effective and cheaply-optimized model. Experiments are conducted on benchmark datasets to evaluate our claims. It shows that the proposed network achieves comparable or better image classification accuracy and training efficiency than traditional DNNs and hierarchical ELMs.

articleTitle: Data Processing and Accuracy Verification of an Airborne Large-Footprint Laser Altimeter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: On December 25, 2017, the National Forestry and Grassland Administration and several scientific research institutes carried out an airborne large spot laser altimetry test in the Xiangxi District of Hunan Province. In this paper, the data processing technologies of laser altimetry were first detailed, and then laser altimetry data error sources were analyzed according to the work flow of the laser altimetry system. Finally, the following experiment was performed: Spots with large errors in the test area were removed, and 45 laser points in flat areas were selected for an accuracy verification test. Next, 100 laser points were selected in the buildings area for a precision verification test. Finally, 6 laser points were randomly selected to compare the relative height extracted from the waveform data with the buildings' measured heights. Study results showed that laser height measurements were very accurate in flat areas and that the extraction method for relative heights from the waveform data was correct and effective.

articleTitle: Research on Cross-Medium Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper designs a type of acoustic buoy for underwater platform to detect the aerial targets crossing the different medium. This cylindrical buoy has a three-dimensional microphone array which is expandable and retractable. In case of storage or launch, the array folds in order to save space and be easy to launch, and the array can expand automatically after the buoy rushes out of the water surface for enlarging the array aperture. This buoy has ability in estimating target direction both in horizontal and vertical. Simulations on the buoy's rising motion are carried out, and the factors influencing launch speed, positive buoyancy effects and ocean currents are analyzed in detail. Experimental results demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed designing method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Beamforming For Jamming Suppression In The Whole Range Domain
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For the traditional early warning radar, only one weight vector is calculated in engineering application for adaptive spatial filtering in a pulse reputation interval (PRI). Therefore, if the training data do not contain the jamming, then the adaptive spatial filtering calculated cannot suppress the jamming. If the adaptive weights update in the whole range domain, the target signal may be contained in the training data, resulting in signal self-cancelling effect. In this paper, we propose a non-homogeneous detector (NHD) based method for updating the adaptive weights in the whole range domain when the training data is contaminated by target signal. The principle is given, and the effectiveness is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Aliasing Error Estimation of Fractional Fourier Transform Based on Windowed Samples
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The fractional powers of the Fourier transform operator is a generalization of the Fourier transform. Although there are many works on the derivation of sampling about fractional Fourier transform, studies on the aliasing error are rare. This paper presents a new aliasing error estimation method of fractional Fourier transform connecting with Poisson sum formula based on windowed samples.

articleTitle: Research on Acoustic Scene Classification Based on Multiple Mixed Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of complex feature extraction and low classification accuracy of traditional acoustic scene classification (ASC) model, this paper proposes a hybrid ASC model based on convolutional neural network (CNN) and long-short-time memory network (LSTM). The convolutional layer in the CNN learns the invariant features from the time-frequency input, the extracted features are input to the LSTM for training, the LSTM units to process the sequence of the extracted features by CNNs. The model finally outputs the result through the classifier. We evaluate the model on UrbanSound8k dataset and analyze which type of the model is more suitable for ASC. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional neural network classification model, the proposed hybrid neural network classification algorithm has better classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on High Resolution Algorithm of Sound Source Localization Based on Microphone Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sound source localization is a far-reaching research topic in the field of acoustics. The microphone array system determined according to a certain geometric topology can effectively locate the sound source. The conventional beamforming (CBF) method has low angular resolution and poor sound source localization. This paper uses a microphone linear array and a microphone planar array by studying the multi-signal classification algorithm (MUSIC) to estimate the orientation of the sound source. The algorithm has high resolution which can make up for the defects of conventional beamforming. Based on the performance simulation of MUSIC algorithm of these two formations, it is found that increasing the number of samples and the signal to noise ratio (SNR) can improve the positioning accuracy of the algorithm. The experimental results show that the performance of the MUSIC algorithm based on the microphone planar array is better than that of the linear array, which can accurately estimate the azimuth angle and elevation angle of the sound source.

articleTitle: PolSAR Image Segment Using Model-Based Decomposition and Energy Minimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The backscattering response of the target is affected by the relative geometric relationship between the target pose and the line of sight of the target and the radar. Ignoring this property, the traditional scattering model-based decomposition method does not interpret the PolSAR image perfectly. The newly proposed model-based six-component scattering matrix power decomposition method (6SD) fully considers the influence of the relative positional relationship between the radar line of sight and the target. It can more accurately acquire the characteristics of the polarized SAR image. In this paper, a PolSAR image classification algorithm combining 6SD and energy minimization is proposed. After obtaining scattering characteristics by model-based six-component scattering matrix power decomposition, the spatial relationship of different pixels is considered to segment the PolSAR image by energy minimization method. In this paper, the principle and specific steps of the algorithm are elaborated in detail, and the proposed algorithm is verified by the measured AIRSAR data. Finally, the experimental results are compared with the wishart classification algorithm. The results show that the proposed algorithm has obvious advantages over the classification using wishart method. The proposed algorithm can make the classification more accurate and make the classification result smoother.

articleTitle: Visual Tracking via Locality-constrained Affine Subspace Coding
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The dictionary plays an important role in the visual tracking whose sample is encoded by a dictionary. However, the dictionary atom is a representative point (visual word) in the previous tracking algorithms. Representative point neglects the geometric manifold structure which the point surrounded by immediately, which leads to limited ability of characterizing the distribution of features on the data manifold. In this paper, we propose a novel visual tracking algorithm with Locality-constrained Affine Subspace Coding (LASC) which explicitly explores the geometric structure of the manifold where these representative points lie. Unlike other encoding methods, LASC formulates the dictionary atom as the subspace attached to the representative point. To further improve the discrimination and diversity of the dictionary, we introduce the weighted spatial information to the representative point. We conduct experiments on challenging benchmarks and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Micro-batch training based on Residual Attention Network for Acoustic Scene Classification with Mismatched Recording Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we provide micro-batch training based on Residual Attention Network for Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC) with mismatched recording devices task. The systems for this task are based on various convolutional networks such as Residual Attention Network due to its excellent performance on image domain. First, we modify the input of the Residual Attention Network so that they operate on the log-mel spectrogram domain of audios. Then, we fine-tune the numbers of layers and kernels to provide better performance for ASC. However, deep learning micro-batch training setup is difficult. For ending this problem, we train Residual Attention Network with Switchable Normalization (SN) and Weight Standardization (WS), respectively. Finally, we verify our method on the TUT Urban Acoustic Scenes 2018 Mobile development dataset, and obtain 0.586 of class-wise accuracy on the dataset. Our best model achieves an improvement of more than 10% in terms of classification accuracy with respect to the Detection and classification of acoustic scenes and events (DCASE) 2018 baseline system.

articleTitle: Analysis and Improvement of General Methods in Infrared Image Detail Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To increase effectiveness and acquire better performance in infrared image visualization, several general methods and the mathematical principles used for detail enhancement are analyzed in this study. In split method, where adopts guided filter to split the image into detail components and base components. Its side effect in compression is brought by increasing detail components' gray value. Then a simplified local processing measure based on image matting is designed to lower the influence. In gradient domain method, a gradient gain factor function is revised resulting from gray value overflow. Meanwhile the method cited solves energy function with high computational complexity and great occupation in memory. In this paper, a matting method is proposed and tested to save more than 30% of time in solving system of linear equations and more than 70 times in matrix storage.

articleTitle: A Network Pruning Method for Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used to improve remote sensing image scene classification performance. However, most of these networks include many parameters and need many computational resources. Which hinders the applications of these networks when facing the satellite, plane or other mobile platforms. In this paper, we introduce a network pruning framework which can reduce the size of the network model and maintain the classification accuracy. In this framework, we train the pruned model using both the original unpruned model's output and training dataset. Which can learn more information than retrain using dataset only. In our experiments, we evaluate our method for remote sensing scene classification on NWPU-RESISC45 dataset. The results demonstrate that our method was effective and maintained the model classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Real-time Object Detection with Attention Mask
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of deep convolutional neural network, the performance of object detection is obviously improved. However, there are still some challenges such as small size and occlusion. In this paper, we present a novel detector named Attention Mask Detector (AMDet). Our motivation is using mask to enhance foreground features and suppress background ones. The mask is produced by an attention branch which is supervised by weak segmentation ground-truth. This weak segmentation ground-truth is generated by bounding box without extra annotations. Our method is based on one-stage detector. We do experiments on both PASCAL VOC and MS COCO datasets and have a result comparison with other one-stage detectors.

articleTitle: Long Distance Commucation Technology of Deep sea Acoustic Release Transponder
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Deep-sea examination and oceanographic surveys have become normally, deep sea acoustic release transponder is an important guarantee for mass laying and reliable release of instruments. This paper proposes pseudo-random code and wideband multiple access technology, which has been used in the self-developed product of 6000m acoustic releaser. The technology increases the processing gain and allows the releaser to communicate robustly over long distances at low signal-to-noise ratios, which is proved by the experimentation the lake and in the sea that the method is effective.

articleTitle: Room temperature single photon emission of colloidal quantum dots at 800nm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Single photon emission at 800 nm from single colloidal quantum dots on a sapphire substrate at room temperature was studied. The fluorescence lifetime, blinking phenomenon and anti-bunching effect of the 800nm colloidal quantum dots were measured, and the second order correlation function g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(0)≈0.035 was obtained, indicating that quantum dots with a center wavelength of 800nm were pure and high-quality single photon sources. It was found that the excitation power had a great influence on the purity of single photon source from the single quantum dots. High laser excitation power would cause the 800nm quantum dots not only exciton emission, but also bi-excitons emission or multi-excitons emission, Accompanying by an increase in the Auger non-radiative recombination and a decrease in the quantum yield. Therefore, it is important to excite the 800nm single quantum dots with proper excitation power.

articleTitle: Robust Minimum Geometric Power Distortionless Response Beamforming with Sparse Constraint in Heavy-tailed Noise of Unknown Statistics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For impulsive noise environment, the adaptive beamformers based on second-order statistics often degrade severely. In this paper, a robust minimum geometric power distortionless response beamforming with sparse constraint is presented for arbitrary algebraically tailed impulsive signal of unknown statistics. The impulsive signal does not have finite second-order and higher order moments due to its property of heavy tails. Unlike the majority of the existing beamformers based on the second-order statistics, the proposed beamforming method minimizes a constrained mixed geometric power and ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm optimization problem. The geometric power effectively characterizes the process strength of the algebraically tailed distribution, while the ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm regularized term enforces the sparsity of the beam pattern. Therefore, the proposed algorithm can provide the potential for improved beamforming capability in the presence of impulse signals. Moreover, two adaptive algorithms, namely, the stochastic gradient (LMS)-based and the recursive least-squares (RLS)-based algorithms, are derived to solve the formulated optimization problem. Additionally, computational complexity analysis is conducted and shows that a comparable complexity between the proposed algorithms and the existing tailed impulsive beamformers. Simulation cases without and with mutual coupling are considered to illustrate that the proposed algorithms are more robust than other popular adaptive beamformers for impulsive signals.

articleTitle: Research on Waveform Design and Imaging of MIMO-SAR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: MIMO SAR, a new type of SAR imaging system, is an effective way to solve the problem of HRWS (high-resolution and wide-swath). The core issue of MIMO SAR is the design of orthogonal waveforms. Microwaves with good-orthogonality, high-coherence, simple transmitting and large time-bandwidth product are beneficial for high-resolution imaging. Both the positive and negative frequency modulated signals and the short-term shift-orthogonal signals are suitable transmit signals for MIMO SAR. In this paper, based on the positive and negative frequency modulated signals and the short-term shift-orthogonal signals, we analyze the imaging performance of the two transmit signals by the correlation functions and imaging results of point targets. On this basis, through the ingenious combination of the positive and negative frequency modulated signals and the short-term shift-orthogonal signals, we design the four orthogonal transmit waveforms for MIMO SAR. The simulation of their correlation functions verifies the effectiveness of the four transmit waveform design.

Author Keywords: positive and negative frequency modulated signal

articleTitle: An Integrated Simulation Platform for Spectrum Cooperation in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) plays an important role in the 5G technology. With the increase of connected vehicles and the growing demand for VANETs, how to utilize the wireless spectrum resources efficiently is particularly important. Spectrum cooperation has become an important direction of VANETs for which simulation is a practical and effective research method. However, most of the existing network simulation software cannot support spectrum level operations. This paper proposes an integrated simulation platform for spectrum cooperation in VANETs that can import real maps and vehicle movement trajectories, provide access to spectrum cooperation algorithms, implement frequency conversion, and display simulation results in various ways. The evaluation results show that the integrated simulation platform can provide real and accurate support for the study of various schemes of VANETs including spectrum cooperation.

articleTitle: Design of Grouped Sensor Geometry in Sky-wave Time-difference-of-arrival Localization Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper studies the design problem of grouped sensor geometry for sky-wave time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) localization systems. The sky-wave TDOA localization system is based on a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenario, where signals are reflected by ionosphere-layer before arriving at sensors. In the literature, the grouped sensor scheme has been proposed to alleviate the impact of ionosphere-layer height (IH) errors, but the geometry design of grouped sensor is still an unsolved problem. In fact, the traditional design methodology is proposed for line-of-sight (LOS) scenarios and relies on special structures of cost function. However, these structures do not exist necessarily in our background. For this reason, we replace the cost function by a simpler version and introduce an additional sensor placement constraint to provide the required structures, which make traditional design methodology applicable. Due to the approximations made during this process, the designed geometries are suboptimal. But it is shown that optimizing over the proposed simpler cost function guarantees that the cramer-rao bound (CRB) will not attain its largest value. Performance comparison validates the novelty of design results.

articleTitle: Extraction and Analysis of Heat Storage Load Characteristics for Power Quality Improvement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the rapid increase of grid-connected capacity of wind turbines in China, wind power consumption is challenged. Especially, the three northern areas' wind curtailment is up to 95% of the whole country. In order to improve the capacity of wind power consumption, our country encourage the technology of clean energy heating. Electrical heating with heat storage is one of the most popular methods of clean energy heating. However, the analysis of the heat storage load is not adequate by the method, because of the huge power grid data, poor data quality and the inaccurate extraction of heat storage load. Aiming the problems, a method based on K-means, K-nearest neighbor algorithm (KNN), and support vector machine algorithm (SVM) is proposed for characteristic extraction of heat storage load in power system. K-means is used to cluster data and extract heat storage load as the training cluster. KNN and SVM are used to train the training cluster and extract the heat storage load. Take the heat storage load in a certain area in Liaoning province as an example. Compared with the traditional methods, the extraction method is more accurate. Then the extracted heat storage data are classified and analyzed. It is of great practical significance to improve the consumption of wind power and improve power quality reasonably.

articleTitle: Performance On The Discrete Variable Based Satellite-to-Ground Quantum Key Distribution Links
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper focuses on evaluating the available secure key lengths of the satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) systems under multiple scenarios. The finite-length secure key rate calculation models are provided for the BB84 and BBM92 based systems, respectively, considering the practical optical link loss. The considered scenarios consist of the solar synchronous orbit satellite scenarios and the walker satellite constellation scenarios. For the BB84 protocol based QKD systems, it is shown that the amount of the secure key reduces slowly as the orbit height grows from 200km to 1100km. Increasing the size of the telescope improves the performance considerably when the deviation of the pointing error is small. However, if the pointing error becomes larger, the benefit from enlarging the telescope size shrinks heavily. On the contrary, the BBM92 protocol based QKD systems are much sensitive to the orbit height and gains much lower performance under the same configurations compared with those under the BB84 protocol. Moreover, the ground station located at higher latitude can achieve better performance than that at lower latitude in the walker satellite constellation with vertical orbital inclination.

articleTitle: An underwater acoustic frequency estimation algorithm based on first-order Newton iterations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of multipath interferences with different doppler frequency offset and the picket fence effect caused by fast Fourier transform, an effective underwater acoustic frequency estimation algorithm based on first-order Newton iterations is proposed in this paper. Bandpass filter is used to coarsely eliminate the multipath interferences with different doppler frequency offset, fast Fourier transform is used to roughly estimate frequency of the direct wave and the estimated frequency value is used as the initial value of first-order Newton iterations to accurately estimate frequency. The frequency estimation error caused by the picket fence effect is greatly eliminated through two iterations, achieving accurate frequency estimation of the direct wave. The good results of simulation (frequency of the transmitted single frequency signal is 10kHz, the sampling frequency is 50kHz and the transmission time is 0.08s) and velocity estimation experiment in a pool (the transmitted frequency was 10kHz, the sampling frequency was 48kHz, the transmission time was 0.1s, the initial horizontal distance and relative moving velocity between the transceiver nodes were 15 m and 1m/s, respectively) verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Airport runway detection based on improved fuzzy clustering for PolSAR images
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a fast airport runway detection method for PolSAR image based on improved fuzzy C-mean method (IFCM). To avoid the issue that FCM is sensitive to random selected class centers, polarimetric scattering characteristics of the targets in PolSAR image are used to generate appropriate initial centers. And a simplified Wishart distance is adopted instead of Euclidean distance in order to obtain a fine classification result. Then, regions of interest which contain runway are automatically extracted from the classification result with the weak scattering characteristic of airport runway. Finally, structural features are used to identify real runway area. Experimental results show that compared with the other two algorithms, the proposed method can detect the airport runway area with more completed structure and less computation time.

articleTitle: Harmonic Retrieval via Low Resolution Sampling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We consider the problem of harmonic retrieval via low resolution sampling, i.e., estimating the parameters of sinusoidal signals in noise from coarse quantized measurement samples. We first derive the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB), i.e., the best performance bound of unbiased estimators, for the sinusoidal parameter estimates. We also introduce a cyclic algorithm for harmonic retrieval from low-bit quantized measurement samples. Numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the cyclic algorithm as compared to the corresponding CRB.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Quantum State Tomography with Compressed Sensing Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Quantum state tomography (QST) is an executable procedure, allowing complete reconstruction of a quantum state. As a basic tool, QST is widely employed in quantum information research. However, many projective measurements on identical copies of the quantum state under test are required in standard QST, which is heavily time-consumed. Here, we perform reconstruction of density matrix with dimensionality of 15×15 by utilizing compressed sensing method at a sampling ratio of 0.35. According to the experimental results, the fidelity could be as high as 93.0%~99.4% and 73.8% for coherent laser beams and heralded single photon sources, respectively.

articleTitle: Weak multi-targets track-before-detect algorithm based on recursive Hough transform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the existing track-before-detect technology based on Hough transform(HT-Tbd) cannot realize the real-time detection of weak multi-target and some targets may be missing detection, a weak multi-target track-before-detect algorithm based on recursive Hough transform is proposed. For the obtained measurement data, firstly, the first <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> frames measurement data is subjected to non-coherent integration detection by using the HT-TBD technology to obtain the initial integration matrix and storage array. Then, the data of 2 ~ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> + 1 frames, 3 - n + 2 frames,… are sequentially subjected to recursive HT-TBD processing, By updating the accumulative matrix and storage array, the data of the previous moment are eliminated and the data of the next time are stored, realizing the recursive detection of each time. Finally, the track correlation is performed according to the detection result of each moment. The algorithm can effectively reduce the amount of calculation and improve the computational efficiency of the method while realizing effective detection of weak multi-targets and avoiding target missing detection.

articleTitle: Covariance Matrix Estimation in Compound-Gaussian Sea Clutter with Discrete Spikes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For adaptive detectors, the presence of discrete sea spikes in sea clutter will lead to remarkable mismatch between the true and estimated value of covariance matrix, especially in higher sea states, thus affecting target detection performance. In order to solve this problem, a new knowledge-aided covariance matrix estimation method based on scene classification is proposed in this paper. The first layer of prior knowledge is the marker information given by sea spike discrimination and extraction results, and the second layer of prior knowledge is provided by long time window of sea spike samples around the cell under test (CUT) and their parameter model. The influence of background nonhomogeneity on covariance matrix estimation is reduced effectively by the method, and verification results with measured sea clutter data indicate that it can improve target detection performance effectively in sea spike background.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of Microwave Landing Radar Used for Deep Space
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: As an important equipment for deep space soft landing, microwave radar provides range and velocity for the probe. Accuracy and operational envelope of range and velocity are key design indexes for landing radar, at the same time, it must be small, lightweight and reliable for deep space exploration. The performance, tested both on ground and in orbit when landing on the moon, is excellent. Based on the telemetry of Chang'e 3 and Chang'e 4 probe, reflectivity of moon surface can be gotten, this will be useful for future detection and microwave radar design.

articleTitle: A Fast Phase Error Correction Method for Compress Sensing SAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a fast phase error correction method for Compress Sensing SAR imaging based on approximated observation. We borrow the idea from the tradition autofocus method, and add a step to first estimate the accurate Doppler frequency rate when building the approximated observation operator. The accurate estimation of Doppler frequency rate will help shrink the difference made by platform motion between the approximated observation and exact observation and thus accelerate the step of phase error correction. First, the approximated observation operators are built by calculating the inverse of Range Doppler Algorithm.
