Then, the approximated observation operators are updated by the accurate estimation of Doppler frequency rate using a Shift-and-Correlation Method. Finally, joint SAR imaging and phase error correction are achieved by solving a two-step optimization problem. The simulation results verify the validity and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The research on data acquisition, processing, and application of multi-type environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Data acquisition in real scenes is a necessary mean to analyze environmental electromagnetic property. In this paper, radar and infrared camera are used as detection sensors. Based on data demand analysis, the experimental process and the experimental scene are carefully designed, the database is founded and data processing and application methods are proposed. The research achievements in this paper provide a reference for further study of big data in remote sensing detection.

articleTitle: Pseudo Independent Conditional Approximation for Training the Mixtures of Gaussian Processes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The mixture of Gaussian processes (MGP) is a powerful probabilistic model for regression and classification. However, how to effectively infer the posteriors and learn the parameters in the model is still a very challenging problem due to the exponential complexity of computation. Although several approximation schemes have been utilized to reduce the computational cost, they usually do not provide reasonable interpretations. In this paper, we first propose a specific variational approximation mechanism for the MGP model in which the joint distribution of latent indicators and latent functions can be factorized as the product of two independent variational distributions. The resulted inference procedure can be well interpreted under the framework of information theory. Inspired by this perspective, we then propose a new approximation method called pseudo independent conditional approximation (PIC) for training the MGP model. It is demonstrated by the experimental results that our proposed training method is more effective than the other existing methods.

articleTitle: Study on Extrapolation Technique of Firefinder Radar Based on Meteorological Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Given the meteorological conditions, especially the issue of low extrapolation accuracy of firefinder radar under high wind speed, we propose a new ballistic trajectory model that takes crosswind and range wind into consideration, to set up the state equations of projectile flight and measurement equations. We also adopt an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) to estimate the parameters through a great deal of datum from trajectory simulation in different fire parameters, and then we yield the simulation results by contrasting and analyzing the Circular Error Probable (CEP) through Fourth-order Ronge-Kutta equations to extrapolate. It is proven by the simulation results that EKF, in consideration of meteorological conditions, is able to enhance the extrapolation accuracy of the firefinder radar.

articleTitle: Instantaneous Frequency Estimation of HFM Signal Based on Interpolated STFRFT-Variable Weight Least Square Fitting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To solve the problem of instantaneous frequency estimation of hyperbolic frequency modulation (HFM) signal under low signal to noise ratio (SNR), a Rife interpolation short-time fractional Fourier transform (STFRFT)-variable weight least square fitting algorithm is proposed. In a certain range of curvature, the fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) is used to better the energy aggregation of the HFM signal. The Rife interpolation is used to improve the estimation accuracy of the instantaneous frequency of the HFM signal. The variable weight least square fitting is used to eliminate the influence of the Rife interpolation abnormal point on the instantaneous frequency estimation and the accuracy is further improved. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by Monte Carlo simulation. The simulation results show that the performance of the algorithm is better than the STFT method.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional angle estimation for sparse MIMO array with velocity receive sensors based on real-valued quadrilinear decomposition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Two-dimensional direction of arrival (DOA) estimation for sparse MIMO array with velocity receive sensors is discussed, and a real-valued quadrilinear decomposition-based method is proposed. The output is firstly transformed into real-valued one via unitary transformation and then the signal subspace is obtained via low-complexity propagator method to shrink the dimension. Thereafter, the data can be fitted into a quadrilinear model, multiple matrices including the direction matrices and velocity matrix can be obtained after the quadrilinear decomposition. By combining the DOA information from these matrices, unambiguous and automatically paired two-dimensional DOA estimation can be obtained. The proposed method only involves real-valued decomposition with low dimension and requires no peak search. Furthermore, it achieves better DOA estimation performance than ESPRIT-like and trilinear decomposition-based methods. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Plane Accuracy Analysis of Multi-source High Resolution Satellite Image
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The Rational Polynomial Coefficients model (RPC) can be used directly to convert image coordinates and object space coordinates without using any satellite physical parameters such as position and attitude. Thus, RPCs are widely accepted by the industry. Based on the RPC model, the present study evaluates the accuracy of different evaluation methods for multi-source China's high-resolution satellite panchromatic images in Hebei Gu-yuan area. The accuracy is evaluated by the Mean Square Error evaluation method and the Circular Error evaluation method. And two methods are compared to get a better accuracy conclusion. The four scene images of this experiment are from Ziyuan-3, Gaofen-1A, Gaofen-1B, and Gaofen-1D satellites. Based on the coordinates of the ground point measured by GPS-RTK, the image coordinates and the artificial image point measurement are subtracted from the object coordinates according to the RPC model, and the results are statistically and accurately analyzed. Experiments show that the accuracy of ZY3-2 satellite imagery is higher than other satellites without ground control point (which surpasses 16.66 panchromatic pixels in the Circular Error evaluation method). Its sensor products have smaller exterior errors. The accuracy of GF-1D satellite imagery is higher than other satellites with ground control point (which surpasses 5.36 panchromatic pixels in the Circular Error evaluation method). It has smaller interior errors in sensor products. In addition, it has significant systematic errors.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Image Change Detection Based on Ground-Based Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multitemporal ground-based imaging radar images have been successfully used for the detection of different types of terrain changes. The image change detection of the ground-based imaging radar is used to estimate the interference change information in the monitoring area within a short time baselines to avoid misjudging the radar deformation image. Many scholars have proposed many effective detection methods for spaceborne radar images, but there are few researches on the change detection method of ground-based imaging radar images. In this paper, a change detection method for ground-based imaging radar image is proposed. To obtain the change information of ground-based imaging radar, the difference map and coherence coefficient map were used to obtain the change region. Experiment results show that the proposed method is effective for ground-based imaging radar image change detection in terms of smooth the background noise and enhance the contrast between the changed and unchanged portions.

articleTitle: Direction Finding of Wideband Signals Using Identically Oriented Vector Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A polarimetric quaternion data alignment based involution stacking approach is proposed to wideband direction finding with identically oriented vector antennas. The signals of interest may come from either noncircular or circular sources. The method is based on the quaternion effective subspace separation technique. It can be viewed as the multi-polarized extension of the uni-polarized aligned rank reduction scheme, fulfilling time domain wideband noncircularity exploitation. Simulation results are included to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Brain Extraction from Magnetic Resonance Imaging Using Deep Neural Network with Edge Prior
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Brain extraction from Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the separation of brain tissue from non-brain tissue in MRI brain images and removal of extra brain tissue. Automatic extraction of brain tissue is an important step in neuroimage processing for clinical applications and scientific research. Accurate delineation of the region can be challenged due to the weak contrast between the brain and non-brain tissue. To overcome this issue, this paper proposed a novel brain extraction approach integrating the boundary information under the deep neural network framework. The boundary of the brain tissues was first detected by an edge detection neural network. The inception module was then utilized in the convolutional stage to capture multi-scale features. A dense decoder shortcut connection structure was finally introduced to leverage the multi-level features in the upsampling stage. The proposed method can achieve Dice overlap coefficients of 98.15% and 98.09%, for the OASIS and LPBA40 datasets respectively. The proposed method outperforms the commonly used brain extraction tools by qualitative and quantitative assessments on two publicly available benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Agent-and-Forward System with Multi-Source and Multi-Relay
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A novel agent-and-forward system with multi-source and multi-relay is designed. In this system, several identical sources transmit analog signals to relay nodes, the destination receives digital signals from relay nodes, so the direct links between the sources and destination are invalid. As a result, relays are used to receive analog signals, and carry on distributed coding to transmit them into digital signals. Subsequently, relays send the digital signals to the destination via wireless channel. Under the help of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) theory, the minimum information rate of multi-relay network is derived, and then a theoretical analysis framework is proposed from combining the minimum information rate and Shannon channel capacity. Finally, the power allocation is optimized under limited system power constraint. Simulation results show that the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) performance of the proposed system will increase with the total system power and the number of the relay nodes. Moreover, when total system power is lower than 10W, the SNR performance of the proposed agent-and-forward system outperforms that of amplify-and-forward (AF) system in the case of the same total power or with the same number of relays.

articleTitle: Horizontal Wavenumber Estimation Technique Based on Compressive Sensing in Shallow Water
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The horizontal wavenumber of normal mode contains environmental information of ocean waveguide, which is an important environmental sensing parameter. To solve the problem of large array aperture requirement and poor resolution performance of the existing horizontal array wavenumber spectrum estimation methods, a horizontal wavenumber estimation technique based on sparse processing is proposed. On the basis of normal mode theory in shallow water, the sparsity of horizontal wavenumber in shallow water is utilized. For the case of coherent and incoherent processing of multiple snapshot data, Basis Pursuit De-Noising(BPDN) and Sparse Bayesian Learning(SBL) methods are used to estimate the horizontal wavenumber. The resolution of horizontal wavenumber spectrum with Sparse Bayesian Learning method is verified to be best through simulation.

articleTitle: An Interacting Multiple Model Smoothing Algorithm for Nonlinear Maneuvering Target Tracking
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of nonlinear maneuvering target tracking system, this paper proposes a novel IMM smoothing algorithm, which can be used in two types of IMM smoothing by changing the delay time of IMM smoother, for nonlinear maneuvering target tracking. The IMM method combined with smoothing algorithm provides more accurate maneuvering target state estimation. The novel IMM smoothing is consisted of forward IMM filtering and backward IMM smoothing. The forward IMM filtering is a standard IMM filter, while the backward IMM smoothing utilizes the updated value and predicted value of the forward IMM filtering to get the smoothing state of the maneuvering target. Simulation results show that the novel IMM smoothing algorithm has better performance compared with the other algorithms.

articleTitle: An Azimuth High Resolution Algorithm Based on Virtual Array and Spatial Resampling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of three-dimensional imaging technology in the field of small target detection, low-frequency imaging sonar with small platform urgently needs high-resolution azimuth algorithm. The azimuth high resolution algorithm of low frequency imaging sonar needs to solve single snapshot and the coherent interference. Conventional spatial smoothing technology has poor decoherence ability when the array aperture is small. To solve these problems, an azimuth high resolution array processing algorithm for low frequency imaging sonar based on virtual array is proposed. The algorithm which combines spatial resampling technology, spatial smoothing technology and the Minimum Variance Distortion Response algorithm (SRMV) to solve the problem of azimuth high resolution imaging of low-frequency three-dimensional imaging sonar in coherent interference environment has been proposed. Because the decoherence ability of spatial smoothing technique is related to the number of array elements, the virtual array technique is used to further improve the decoherence and stability of the SRMV algorithm in this paper. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has better decoherence ability. The sea test data show that the azimuth imaging resolution of the proposed algorithm is significantly improved than that of the conventional beam method under the same physical aperture, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Robust Adaptive Beamforming for Distributed Radar Based on Covariance Matrix Reconstruction and Steering Vector Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the high dynamic characteristics of the airborne distributed radar, array errors cannot be avoided, thus the performance of the conventional adaptive beamforming methods will deteriorate severely. In order to solve this problem, a robust adaptive beamforming method based on covariance matrix reconstruction and steering Vector estimation is proposed for the airborne distributed radar. In the proposed method, an annulus uncertainty set is used to constrain the interference steering vector, and then the Capon spectrum is integrated on the surface of the region to obtain interference-plus-noise covariance matrix. Afterwards, the iterative robust Capon beamformer is used to obtain a more accurate estimation of the desired signal steering vector. Finally the weight vector is calculated by using the estimated interference-plus-noise covariance matrix and the desired signal steering vector. As the interference-plus-noise covariance matrix is well reconstructed by the annulus uncertainty set and the signal steering vector is calibrated, the proposed method is both robust to array structure errors and signal angle errors compared with the existing methods. The robustness and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm are verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Real-Time Object Detection With Densely Connected Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we are interested in the object detection problem with high accuracy and fast prediction. To achieve this, we have modified the existing object detection algorithm, we design a new feature extraction network, predict detection target based on multiple feature maps and improve the anchor box. Particularly, since DenseNet can combine the output of previous convolutional layers by using skip connection operation to make prediction more accurate, we introduce DenseNet to improve the YOLOv3-Tiny network. Furthermore, we add a prediction layer to the improved network to detect more true targets. Finally, we clustered the ground truth of specific dataset to get the anchor box for training to improve the detection results of the improved network. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our network by using Pascal VOC datasets. The experimental results show that the improved network increases the detection accuracy by 14% and the detection speed is 63 frames per second in the video detection. The detection accuracy is improved to a higher level and the detection speed still meeting the real-time detection requirement, which shows that the proposed method is robust and effective. Anchor box, DenseNet, Video detection

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis for Inertial Devices Based on Variational Mode Decomposition and Probabilistic Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A real-time fault diagnosis method for inertia device based on variational mode decomposition is proposed to ease the difficulty of fault recognition for slow-varying output. The correlative modal components related to output data of inertia device are calculated by variational mode decomposition method firstly, subsequently the number of modal components is confirmed adaptively with frequency discrimination, then the mapping strategy from modal components to fault eigenvector is defined, trustworthy fault diagnostic capability is built with fault classifier based on probabilistic neural network at last. Multiple fault diagnosis simulation is carried out with average correct rate at least 80%. Considering there is no need for the operating principle of the inertia device to participate in the diagnosis process, the fault diagnosis method can be applied in launch vehicles in order to supplement approaches for health state assessment of inertia devices.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of Satellite Image Target Recognition Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Space remote sensing technology is one of the most important means to acquire ground information at present. In recent years, due to the progress of remote sensing satellite level, the secondary development technology of image recognition, target classification, information extraction and surveillance for ships on the sea has become the focus of research. the convolution neural network algorithm is used to construct of the ship satellite image target recognition network. The convolution neural network model is built by synthesizing the parameter characteristics of the data set. The standard data set and encapsulated ship satellite image target data set are used for training and testing. According to the test results, the convolution neural network has a good ability to recognize ship satellite image target, which proves that the convolution neural network structure is feasible and has a good research and application value.

articleTitle: A Chinese Speech Recognition System Based on Articulatory Features
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we build a Chinese speech recognition system based on acoustic features and articulatory features (AFs). We modify the original Chinese phonemes and define several language-independent AF groups based on International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) and linguistic knowledge. To eliminate the need to force alignment information and simplify training, a technique using connectionist temporal classication (CTC) criterion is adopted. The Mandarin speech recognition system is built by the joint features which are concatenated with AFs and MFCC. The results show that using of AFs can improve the performance of ASR task on THCHS-30 30 hours data set.

articleTitle: The Micro-Doppler Features Extraction of Experimental Data of Chaff Cloud Scatter Dispersion Based on Empirical Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This article studies the micro- Doppler characteristics of chaff cloud scatter based on the chaff filaments dispersion experiments. This paper highlights the extraction method of micro-Doppler features using the Empirical Mode Decomposition method incorporated with time-frequency analysis method. In order to extract the characteristics, the scattering signal is decomposed into a set of intrinsic-mode functions that are represented at different scales. The components are then reconstructed and analyzed by adopting the Short-Time Fourier Transform. After the separation of the Doppler frequency of the unexpanded chaff cluster radar return, the micro-Doppler frequency and micro- motion parameters of chaff filaments are estimated. The results of the experiment show that this extraction method has been successfully adopted to obtain the micro- Doppler features of chaff filaments. And a conclusion has been proved that the period of micro-Doppler frequency is determined by the period of chaff filaments vibration.

articleTitle: Measuring multiscale complexity in human sleep electroencephalography
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Increasing reports indicated that multiscale fashion is a general and efficient approach to investigate various of natural and physiological states. In this work, a generalization of the q-complexity-entropy curve in the multiscale fashion (GMCE curve) is introduced. In addition, the concept of the minimum permutation entropy and the maximum statistical complexity are proposed to allow the intuitive visualizations of entropy/complexity in the multiscale fashion, so-called generalized multiscale permutation entropy (GMPE), which is proposed to yield a spectrum of entropies and complexities. The proposed GMCE curve and/or the GMPE method is shown capable of identifying if an irregular oscillation is either chaotic or randomly distributed, as well as if it is highly predictable or long-term correlated. In the sleep analyses, both the minimum permutation entropy and the maximum statistical complexity present significant differences across sleep stages (p <;. 0001*), whereas all five sleep stages are differentiable in the multiple comparisons. The proposed methods facilitated the investigations of irregular oscillations with generalization in timescales and Tsallis q-entropy.

articleTitle: Analytical solution of active noise control in sound field with a reflective surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The active noise control in half-free space is different from that of free space due to the existence of reflective surface. In this paper, an analytic solution model of half-free field active control system is presented. The model regards the loudspeaker and its mirror loudspeaker on the ground as a dipole in the same direction, so that its directivity distribution in the sound field can be calculated. When the location of primary source and secondary source is fixed, the model can provide the locations which are not suitable for placement of error points. The cut-off height and cut-off frequency of active control in half-free field are also provided.

articleTitle: A Fast State-Space Algorithm for 3D Scattering Center Extraction of Radar Targets
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Scattering centers play a very important role in applications such as radar target recognition. Extracting the scattering center position parameters during target reconstruction can also greatly reduce the amount of data that need to be stored. The state-space algorithm forms a Hankel matrix by spatial sliding in each direction, then extracts the scattering center coordinate information by three times singular value decomposition, although the precision is high but the time consuming is too much. This paper proposes an optimized fast state-space algorithm, which only needs to compute the singular value decomposition for one time. And based on the GTD model, position coordinates of the scattering center can be directly obtained in this paper. Just one time singular value decomposition reduces the time consuming by this algorithm, and the simulation results show that the precision of this algorithm is also high.

articleTitle: A Phase Adjustment Method for Compensating Doppler Migration in Passive Bistatic Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Increasing coherent integration time is a conventional approach to improving the detection ability of passive bistatic radar (PBR). However, due to the maneuverability of the moving target, the problem of Doppler migration will be caused by phase errors introduced during the long coherent time, resulting in the loss of detection ability. Aiming at solving this problem, the reflected signal model of the system is derived firstly. Then the influence of the target maneuverability on the performance of the traditional target detection algorithm is analyzed. Further, a phase correction technique is developed for compensating the Doppler migration in the PBR. Phase errors are estimated by iteratively solving an equation which is derived by minimizing the mean recovery error (MRE) of the reconstructed target based on the principle of the fixed-point iteration technique. Since no assumption is made during the derivation, the proposed technique is nonparametric, and it could be used to compensate any form of the phase error. Theoretical analysis and simulation confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Data Augmentation using Conditional Generative Adversarial Network for Underwater Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In underwater target recognition tasks, a deep learning recognition model is more effective than traditional methods, but meanwhile requires sufficient labeled data at the same time. Data augmentation is an effective method to increase the size of training data and reduced the mismatch between training and test. Different from the traditional approaches by directly adding noise to the original waveform or perform waveform transformation, we explore a supervised conditional generative adversarial network framework for data augmentation by using few ship data. The experiment result shows that higher recognition accuracy can be obtained when generated data are added to the original data. We find that the recognition models do not always perform better when the added generated data increases. It is appropriate to add about 5 times of the amount of the original data. The experimental result shows that in 5-target recognition task, with only 1000 samples for each type of target provided, a relative 8.8% to 13.3% improvement can be obtained when adding the generated data.

articleTitle: Robust End to End Acoustic Model Based on Deep Similarity Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Automatic speech recognition has shown tremendous progress over the pass decade and many methods have been proposed for speech recognition under noise-free environment. However, these algorithms suffer from performance degradation in the presence of acoustic interference. In this paper, a new robust speech recognition model is proposed to tackle this problem. To improve the generalization capability of the model, the idea of parameter sharing between clean speeches and noisy ones is suggested. Furthermore, the similarity loss term is also proposed to enclose the feature results generated from clean and noisy samples for further recognition. Meanwhile, the Connectionist Temporal Classification approach is employed to label unsegmented sequences, making the model feasible for robust end-to-end recognition. Several types of noises from different speech databases are employed to evaluate the recognition performance, and the experimental results show that the proposed model is less sensitivity to acoustic inference and more robust to noises.

articleTitle: Clutter Cancellation for Radar Detecting Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Based on FPLMS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A Frequency-domain Pulse Least-Mean-Square (FPLMS) algorithm is proposed to cancel clutter for radar detecting Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV), which are masked by the broadened Doppler main lobe of clutter. Making use of the stationarity of clutter across pulses, this algorithm adaptively estimates the complex amplitudes of clutter in all range cells, reconstructs clutter and then cancels them from echo signal. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is able to cancel clutter effectively and thus eliminate the mask effect of clutter main lobe on slow targets. In addition, the filter notch of the proposed algorithm is quite narrow, about 1/3 width of the traditional Moving Target Identification (MTI) filter. For targets with velocity greater than one velocity resolution cell, there are almost no Signal-Noise-Ratio (SNR) losses.

articleTitle: Automatic Digital Recognition of Multiple Electricity Dashboards
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Intelligent detection of electric transmissions and distribution equipment is impeded by factors such as the potential diversity of displays, the vulnerability of meter digits reading, and the slow speed of training and predicting. To deal with the problem, this paper aims to use the technology of pattern recognition to automatically recognize various kinds of digital displays by analyzing images collected by a CCD camera. To be more specific, firstly, we design a multi-layer convolutional module to classify different types of dashboards. Secondly, to deal with different types of dashboards, we presents an improved Adaboost algorithm in the training process that can quickly identify and cut out the display area of the meters. Lastly, we implement several digital image processing algorithms to recognize the dashboard readings accurately. The experimental results show that our method performs well in improving recognition precision.

articleTitle: Research on the Radio Frequency Simulation Method for Wide-band Radar Complex Target based on Physical Optics and Physical Diffraction Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A radio frequency (RF) simulation technique based on high frequency hybrid method is proposed for complex target. Firstly, the radar cross section (RCS) of the target is obtained by vector addition of facets scattering field and wedges scattering field that are calculated respectively by physical optics (PO) method and physical theory of diffraction (PTD). Then, scattering centers of the target are extracted based on multi scattering center theory, and the radar echo signal is simulated through radio frequency simulation system (RFSS). This technique could improve the fidelity of radar signal simulation and the confidence of RF simulation test. At last, simulation results validate the technique.

articleTitle: Keynote Speeches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the keynote presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Noncontact Detection of Heartbeat and Respiratory Rate via 77GHz Radar Based on Adaptive Double Sliding-Time Window Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In radar-based vital sign monitoring, it's a challenge to keep the trade-off between high accuracy and real-time processing capability. To offer an effective approach towards this challenge and achieve noncontact detection of human heartbeat and respiratory rate, this paper proposes a joint time-frequency detection algorithm. This algorithm bases on adaptive double sliding-time window (ADSW) technology using both fast Fourier transform (FFT) and time domain searching-peak (TSP) methods to perform preliminary detection. Then adaptive weighting is utilized to adjust the lengths of next data sliding windows dynamically and obtain the final output from previous detection results. In the meanwhile, the chosen weighting factors are determined by signal characteristics such as the short average energy (SAE) and zero-crossing rate (SAZC), which can improve the real-time capability as well as maintain good accuracy. Finally an experiment was carried out and the proposed algorithm achieved good results.

articleTitle: Logo Detection Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Logo detection processing is a popular application in images. However, due to sample variety in illumination, occlusion, rotation, and scale, the appearance of logos varies greatly, which is challenging for logo detection. In this paper, we propose a novel logo detection method based on the global pyramid text attention module. The global pyramid text attention module (GPTAM) contains the Global Text Attention Module(GTAM) and the Pyramid Text Attention Module (PTAM). GTAM can take use of the context information of texts in logos to reduce detection error, and PTAM can handle logos with multiple scales. We use non-maximum suppression(NMS) method in the postprocessing to obtain the final detection. The experiments on FlickrLogos-32 and TopLogos-10 databases demonstrate that our proposed outperforms the state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, our method also achieves better or comparable performance on ICDAR2013 and ICDAR2015 datasets for scene text detection.

articleTitle: A novel methodology of cardiac arrhythmia classification based on ECG and context-dependent HMM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel diagnosis method for the classification of cardiac arrhythmia based on electrocardiogram (ECG). The recognition of abnormal heart beat was performed using the context-independent hidden Markov model (HMM) and context-dependent HMM. Gaussian mixture model (GMM) was used as the state emission probability density function. The input feature of the recognition system was the raw heartbeat waveform. There were no other feature transform steps. Six classes of heartbeats, including normal beat, paced beat, left bundle branch block beat, right bundle branch block beat, premature ventricular contraction, and ventricular escape beat, were categorized by the system. The performance was evaluated on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database and the European ST-T Database. The experimental results showed that the context-dependent HMM was more precise than the context-independent HMM. The context-dependent HMM system achieved a mean level of 95.26%, 90.67% and 95.60% in heart beats recognition accuracy, sensibility and specificity respectively. The results confirmed the importance of the generative model and the raw waveform feature strategy in ECG study.

articleTitle: Research on Step Response Characteristics of Flexible DC Fiber-Optic Current Transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to meet the high-speed response requirements of DC fiber-optic current transformer (FOCT) in flexible DC transmission engineering, the step response characteristics of DC FOCT and its dynamic performance improvement methods are studied. The discrete mathematical model of DC FOCT is established and analyzed by simulation. The key parameters affecting the step response characteristics of DC FOCT are transit time, forward channel gain, filter order, and communication delay. A step response test platform for DC FOCT is built, and the step response characteristics of DC FOCT are tested. The experimental results are consistent with the simulation analysis. It is shown by experimental results that the step response rise time of the DC FOCT is less than 40μs after parameter optimization, meeting the relevant application requirements.

articleTitle: Neural Networks from a Physical Perspective
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The investigations on neural networks have attracted a broad interest from lots of research communities in recent years. The evidences of their advantage over traditional methods are found when they are applied to dealing with plenty of practical tasks. However, challenges still remain in the topics, such as understanding the mathematical reason of their effectiveness. Here, we review some of the recent works and present a new look on the neural network from a physical perspective.

articleTitle: Wideband Phase-Only Transmit Adaptive Digital Beamforming Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: To create nulls in the transmit pattern of a array antenna to suppress external interference and clutter, modern phased array radar systems usually use phase-only modulation to provide acceptable null depths. At present, most proposed phase algorithms are developed for narrowband applications. This paper describes a wideband phase-only transmit adaptive digital beamforming (ADBF) scheme. Firstly, an amplitude-phase weighted wideband transmit ADBF algorithm based on the multiple linear constrained minimum variance (MLCMV) criterion is derived. On this basis, the optimal phase-only weighted solution is obtained by re-iteration uniform weight optimization (RUWO). The validity of the scheme is proved by theoretical analysis and simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Building Areas Detection From Optical Remote Sensing Images Based on Hierarchical Structure Description
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Automatically detection of suburban building areas(BA) is one of the research hotspots in the field of remote sensing image(RSI), which is widely used in land monitoring and anti-terrorism. However, due to the large differences in the appearance of suburban buildings, the mainstream methods are difficult to obtain better detection results. To address these problems, this paper presents an hierarchical structure description suburban building areas detection framework, which can be divided into two main stages: (1)in the stage of extraction of key structure(s)(KS), we propose a candidate screen method based on roof parallel structure(RPS), to achieving rapid extraction KS. (2)in the stage of candidate region identification, we present a Deformation Adaptability Model, this model can make full used of the relationship between key structures of buildings, and it has better adaptability to distributed target. We test the proposed method on both ordinary and complex structure data sets, and the experimental results demonstrate that our framework can achieve high accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Fast Satellite Selection Algorithm for GPS / BD Integrated Navigation System Based on K-means++ Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The GPS/BD integrated navigation system improves the positioning accuracy and reliability compared with the single system, but makes the calculation amount increase exponentially. In order to improve the real-time performance of the integrated navigation system, a fast satellite selection algorithm based on K-means++ clustering algorithm is proposed. After preferentially selecting a satellite with the highest elevation angle, the method performs K-means++ clustering algorithm on the remaining satellites, and then selects one satellite in each cluster to obtain the final satellite selection combination. The simulation results show that the probability of GDOP less than 2.5 obtained by this method is approximately 100%, and the probability that the difference between the method and the traditional GDOP satellite selection method less than 0.1 is 94.3%, but the time is reduced by 99.11%. It is proved that the method greatly improves the real-time performance while satisfying the positioning accuracy.

articleTitle: Clustering Based Interference Analysis of GSM-R Network on Drive Test Data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The traditional method of analyzing and processing the drive test (DT) data to find the interferences in the Global System for Mobile Communications-Railway (GSM-R) network is often a manual method, which is not only inefficient, but also difficult to find the correlation and regularity among the DT data. In order to improve the efficiency of capturing interferences in GSM-R network and to discover the regularity of the DT data, we propose a method to capture and analyze the interferences in GSM - R network based on DT data clustering. Firstly, we design and implement a software system of DT terminal to acquire DT data sets. Then, we use the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) clustering algorithm to analyze the DT data and initially determine the location of the interferences in GSM-R network. Finally, according to the analyzed results, we conduct an interference check and successfully find the interference source. The method provides a reference for the future research of drive test data.

articleTitle: Design of Distributed Heterogeneous General Signal Processing Platform Architecture
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Firstly, by analyzing the demand of electronic information system capabilities in complex battlefield environment, a distributed heterogeneous general signal processing platform architecture is designed. It focuses on the overall structure and composition, hardware architecture and software architecture. The platform adopts open system architecture, which can realize the decoupling of functional software and hardware platform, task mode and implementation. Secondly, technology implementation approach is discussed in three respects, including resource virtualization management, parallel scheduling and real-time interconnection in heterogeneous environments, and autonomous mission planning. Finally, the characteristics of the architecture are summarized.

articleTitle: Ground Target Automatic Recognition and Tracking in Complex Battlefield Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the developments of science and the changes of modern warfare modes, the precise guidance and attack towards hostile targets in complex battlefield environments has extremely important military needs and research significance. However, the existing guidance mode is often constrained by factors such as battlefield background interference, target appearance variation and limited data links, which in turn affects tracking and strike performance. To this end, we present an integrated recognition and tracking scheme for the ground targets in complex battlefield environment. Specifically, with the missile-target distance information, we design an adaptive scale estimation scheme to tackle the aspect ratio variation during tracking. Furthermore, an efficient tracking monitoring index is advocated to judge the tracking condition as well as forecast the potential tracking failure. Once tracking failure is determined, a deep-learning based detection module is activated to re-detect the target as well as correct the tracking drift. In the strike stage of the mission, the key region of the hostile target would be identified and locked by the missile in order to maximize the attack effect. The proposed recognition and tracking scheme are tested upon extensive actual videos and achieved a tracking accuracy over 85%, which demonstrates its effectiveness as well as provides a novel solution for accurate and robust attack on enemy targets in a complex battlefield environment.

articleTitle: Target detection algorithm for Airborne Radar based on Map Information
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Due to the strong ground clutter, there will be much land false alarms for airborne radar when detecting the sea target on the sea-land boundary, which will severely degrade the radar's detection performance. In this paper, a new target detection algorithm for airborne radar based on map information is proposed. In the proposed framework, the longitude and latitude information of the radar detection area was calculated first, using the carrier aircraft attitude data provided by inertial navigation system. Then the sea-land information based on the longitude and latitude was searched on the map data, aiming to realize the sea-land segmentation and get the sea-land. The target detection process was implemented based on the sea-land contour map. The proposed algorithm is experimentally validated using the real echo data, indicating that the proposed framework can recognize the target's sea-land position exactly and help selecting or eliminating targets as demanded, which can significantly reduce the false alarm rate and improve the radar's detection performance.

articleTitle: Joint DOD and DOA Estimation for Bistatic MIMO Radar with Unknown Spatially Colored Noise: A Tensor Completion Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we stress the problem of joint direction-of-departure (DOD) and direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for bistatic multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar in the presence of unknown spatially colored noise. By utilizing the sparse structure of the noise covariance as well as the lower-rank tensor property of the signal counterpart, a tensor completion approach is presented for de-noising. Thereafter, joint DOD and DOA estimation is accomplished via the tensor subspace technique. Unlike the state-of-the-art spatial correlation method, the proposed method would not hurt the virtual aperture of MIMO radar, and it achieves more accurate estimation performance than the existing methods. Numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of our algorithm.

articleTitle: One Narrowband Cross-Correlator Detector for Passive Sonar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The broadband cross-correlator detector can effectively improve the bearing resolution of multi-targets. But the broadband cross-correlator detector can not obviously provide underwater targets with abundant line spectrum because the frequency spectrum was normalized by the power of every frequency.In this paper, a narrowband cross-correlator detector is proposed by which the frequency lines were phase binning processed. After the frequency lines were automatically detected in all preformed beams, they were placed in appropriate beams. The appropriate beam was selected by phase comparison for frequency line using the phase difference between the left and right beam outputs of the split array. The theoretical analysis and simulation result show that this method could get a better detection performance via the line spectrum component for passive sonar, meanwhile the bearing resolution can be obviously improved. The processing result of the sea-trial data shows the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: An ADS-B Anti-counterfeiting System Based on TDOA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The ADS-B signal is not encrypted in any form, and traditional receivers cannot verify the authenticity of the ADS-B signal, which poses a potential risk to aviation safety. Considering the insecurity of ADS-B, this paper proposes a four-station passive multilateration ADS-B anti-counterfeiting system based on TDOA. A reference station is used to synchronize the clock of each station, and the Chan Algorithm is used for solving TDOA equations. We have built the system and tested it in the real-world with several flights near Beijing Capital International Airport. The system can track the plane route in real time and compare it with the positions claimed by ADS-B messages to achieve the purpose of ADS-B anti-counterfeiting and pseudo signals localization.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Networks for Exo-atmospheric Infrared Objects Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: External atmospheric infrared (IR) target recognition is an important research topic of space surveillance systems. The different micromotion states of the target result in respective features in the obtained sequence of IR radiation intensities, and such differences are difficult to visually describe and difficult to extract efficiently. Due to the difficulty of spatial experiments, the target sample data is very limited. In the case of limited labeled samples, there are few methods that can effectively classify time series effectively, resulting in low classification accuracy and difficulty in meeting practical application requirements. We use generative adversarial networks(GAN) for semi-supervised learning, combining neural network classifiers with adversarial generation models for the classification of infrared grayscale time series of spatial targets. The effective classification of the target is achieved with a small number of labeled target samples. The experiment proves the effectiveness of the method and the classification effect is better than other methods.

articleTitle: Dual-frequency correlation back projection algorithm using the dual-frequency GRP to detect the defects of tunnel structure nondestructively
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The detection of defects of tunnel structure from surface-based geophysical reflection data is an interesting question in ground-penetrating radar (GPR) research. There are many studies have been executed to effectively solve this problem. But the resolution and accuracy of the results are still inadequate to meet the requirements of detection. Here we present newly developed dual-frequency GPR equipment and imaging algorithm for nondestructive detection of tunnel structure. The imaging algorithm called dual-frequency correlation back projection (DCBP) algorithm is based on dual-frequency radar data. The dual-frequency GPR equipment works well according to the results of test. And our work importantly confirms recent simulation-based findings that DCBP algorithm can bring remarkable signal-to-noise ratio enhancement and suppress the influence of multi-reflection. So it can offer the precise location information of anomalies. Finally we applied the method in the nondestructive detection at 790th~800th rings of International Passenger Center Station of Shanghai rail transit line 12. The concrete lining and steel bar are clearly visible. And the information of thickness of grouting and void in the grouting layer are provided. The actual results appear however very promising.

articleTitle: Impact analysis of CFAR detection for false targets generated by the phase-switched screen
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The phase-switched screen (PSS) has been proved effective in the application of shielding a target or deceiving the radar system when the modulation frequency of it is set greater or smaller than the signal bandwidth. This paper analyses impacts of false targets generated by PSS (PSS-decoys) echoes on radar constant false alarm rate detection. The generation principle of PSS-decoys and the key factors that influence the signatures of PSS-decoys are introduced briefly at first. On base of it, the detection cost caused by the false alarm and false dismissal in a search period of radar is chosen as the criteria of detection performance. The detection costs of CA-CFAR, OS-CFAR, CMLD-CFAR detectors under multiple decoys jamming environment are analysed. Specially, we investigate the influence of the PSS key factors on detection costs from the perspective of simulation. The results show that detection costs will increase remarkably due to false targets existing and it is sensitive to the switching frequency, and the relationship to the duty ratio is tightly relevant to SNR. Among three detectors, the detection costs of CMLD-CFAR detector are higher than that of adopting CA-CFAR and that of adopting OS-CFAR.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Joint Learning for Chinese Word Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, some methods of learning Chinese word embedding based on the characters and sub-characters information have been proposed and achieve state-of-art results. Generally speaking, good embedding of characters and sub-characters can help learn better embedding of words. However, current methods utilizing characters and sub-characters information, such as character-based CWE and sub-character-based JWE, only learn embedding of characters and sub-characters by predicting the target word. We believe it's not enough to improve the quality of characters and sub-characters embedding, so we propose a method called HJWE which predicts the target word, characters and sub-characters in the target word at the same time. The experiment result shows that our method performs best on the word similarity, word analogy and text classification tasks.

articleTitle: Modulation recognition of space-time block codes based on Fourth-order delay matrix
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to identify the modulation mode of STBC signal in frequency selective fading channel, an improved STBC modulation recognition algorithm based on fourth-order time delay moment is proposed in the condition of single receiving antenna. This algorithm calculates the fourth-order delay moment of spacetime block code at the receiving end, and uses threshold detection method to compare the estimated value of fourth-order delay moment with the threshold interval of theoretical value, and automatically identifies the modulation mode of signal. Simulation results show that the algorithm is not affected by adverse factors such as frequency deviation and phase jitter, and there is little difference between different STBC recognition effects.

articleTitle: The research on acoustic communication anti-doppler shift technology based on FrFFT
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Underwater acoustic communication technology plays an important role in underwater applications, but the sound velocity v0 in underwater acoustic channel is much lower than the propagation velocity c0 in electromagnetic wave in the air. It is assumed that the velocity of the platform is v, i.e. v/v0>> v/c0 makes the influence of the velocity of the platform in the underwater acoustic channel on the Doppler shift of the receiver far greater than the influence of the electromagnetic wave mobile platform in the air on the receiver channel. In this paper, a joint channel coding and decoding method based on LFM-FrFFT (Linear Frequency Modulation- Fast Fourier Transform) is proposed. The receiver system decodes the communication system by detecting the up-and-down frequency sweep of the LFM. Due to the doppler insensitivity of the LFM signal, the FrFft can effectively detect the LFM signal through the fractional-order domain to solve the Doppler-induced receiver channel mismatch problem.

articleTitle: Sound Signal Separation Technique in Wind Tunnel Test by Using Planar Microphone Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The traditional nearfield acoustic holography (NAH) requires free field on the side of the hologram plane back to the target sound source. There are often acoustic reflection and scattering caused by the interference source or the wall in the wind tunnel test, which greatly limits the application of NAH. By processing the sound signal measured by the planar microphone array, the target source and the interference source can be separated to achieve the purpose of indirectly removing the background interference. Aiming at the situation that the target sound source and the hologram are located inside and outside the wind tunnel jet respectively, combined with the convective wave equation solution in moving fluid medium and the classical shear layer correction theory, the spatial Fourier transform-based separation using single hologram is corrected. The target sound source inside the jet and the interference sound source outside the jet are separated, leading to the acoustic parameters of the target sound source acting on the hologram plane alone. Numerical simulations show that the change of working parameters has little effect on the separation results. The separation errors under different conditions are small, and the method has a certain anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of reconstruction algorithm based on non-uniform sampling system
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For sparse ultra-wideband signals in frequency domain, the non-uniform adoption system is used to sample the signals at different rates. OMP algorithm, LASSO algorithm and BCS algorithm are used to recover the non-uniformly sampled signal. According to the analysis and comparison of the simulation results, the following conclusions are drawn: BSC algorithm has little change in time-consuming and robustness with the increase of the number of observations, and has better reconstruction performance when the number of observations is low and the noise is included.

articleTitle: Toeplitz-Based Underwater Acoustic Channel Blind Deconvolution
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a blind channel deconvolution method based on the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO). Using a Toeplitz structured formulation of the received signal, we form an iterative blind deconvolution scheme, alternatively estimating the underwater impulse response, and alternatively the transmitted waveform. The resulting optimizations are convex, and we formulate a computationally efficient solver using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). We illustrate the performance of the resulting estimator using both simulated and measured underwater signals.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Image Fusion Method Based on Adaptive Fractional Differential
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to resolve the issues of spectral distortion and lack of details in image fusion, a new remote sensing image fusion method based on adaptive fractional differential is proposed, which can dynamically enhance the remote sensing image according to different image features. Firstly, up-sampling operation is used in multispectral image, and the multispectral image is transformed by IHS transformation to obtain luminance component. Secondly, panchromatic image and luminance component are enhanced by adaptive fractional differential. Next, the enhanced luminance component and panchromatic image are integrated to obtained a new image, and then the new image is dealt with by histogram matching. Finally, the fused image is reconstructed by adopting the inverse IHS transformation. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method can enhance the details and textures while preserving spectral information and smooth areas in image fusion. The proposed method outperforms other traditional fusion algorithms both in visual effect and objective evaluation indexes.

articleTitle: Processing of Millimeter Wave Airborne Interferometric SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Compared to other wave bands, interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) system employed millimeter wave equipment is capable of providing finer spatial resolution and higher measurement accuracy with smaller volume and lighter weight. However, the shorter wave length, which is more sensitive to the range error, also brings some problems in SAR/InSAR data processing. In this paper, a complete processing chain is investigated to generate high-precision digital elevation model (DEM) starting from the millimeter wave radar raw data. Experimental results obtained by the proposed approach are presented and discussed with the real measured airborne millimeter wave SAR data.

articleTitle: Building Layout Determination Based on Generative Adversarial Nets in Through-Wall Radar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For through-wall radar imaging (TWRI), the building layout determination is an essential task in practice applications. In this paper, two multi-input multi-output (MIMO) radar with 8 transmitting antennas and 2 receiving antennas under two vertical views are deployed to finish detection, and the generative adversarial nets (GAN) is applied to finish building layout determination. The electromagnetic simulations demonstrate that the GAN achieves great performance in building layout determination.

articleTitle: Adaptive Ensemble Embedding for Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this work, we present an approach for transfer learning. Many adversarial transfer learning approaches train merely one domain classifier to differentiate the features as either source domain or target domain and train a feature generator to perplex the discriminator. One problem exists with this family of approaches, where the single discriminator is used to differentiate the features as source or target thus could not mine the hard samples. To solve the above problem, we introduce a new adaptive ensemble embedding scheme for transfer learning (AEETL). We propose to learn multiple adaptive embedding features with considering the hard samples for transfer learning. AEETL mainly contains two components: (1) the weight module is applied to predict the adaptive ensemble weights; (2) the ensemble module is applied to mine the hardness of samples following a coarse-to-fine scheme. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of our approach.

articleTitle: Accuracy Analysis of Multi-Aperture Along-track Interferometric SAR for Ocean Surface Current Vector Mapping
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ocean surface current vector, including the magnitude and direction, is very valuable for many applications. The multi-aperture along-track interferometric (MA-ATI) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) provides a new solution for the measurement of ocean current vector. However, if the MA-ATI method tends to play the greatest role in practical application, the accuracy of measurement must be considered and analyzed first. In this paper, the influence of system parameters and ocean current variation on the accuracy of MA-ATI method is studied by establishing a performance evaluation model, which lays a foundation for the wide application of MA-ATI method in current vector detection.

articleTitle: A High Resolution SF-LFM Radar System based on USRP X310
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a step-frequency linear-frequency-modulation (SF-LFM) radar for high resolution ranging and imaging based on USRP X310 equipped with UBX-160 daughter-boards. A wideband LFM baseband signal is adopted in this platform because of its high quality of amplitude and frequency characteristics while can be easily generated by digital techniques and match filter processing is used while it's insensitive to doppler shift of echo data. The transmitting signal is divided into two channels through power divider, one channel is transferred to transmitting horn antenna through amplifier, and the other is transferred directly to the receiver. The receiving signal at each step frequency band is deconvoluted by using inverse filter technique while the receiving signal of second channel is regarded as reference signal. A reflection spectrum reconstruction method is proposed to synthesize wideband response signal and a one-dimensional distance image can be obtained. With the movement of Tx/Rx, a B-scan radar profile can be obtained and 2-dimensional image can be obtained.

articleTitle: The Circular Array PASI Algorithm Based on Array Translation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Based on the iteration of array data which is derived from the subarray, the pilot-aided subarray iterative (PASI) algorithm estimates the Direction of Arrival (DOA) using the pilot signals. While existing PASI algorithms can handle situations of multiple signal sources and multipath precisely and accurately, application in DOA estimation with circular arrays is beyond their capabilities. Considering this case, this paper proposes a circular PASI algorithm based on array translation and discusses influencing factors with simulation respectively. Simulation results show that situations of multiple signal sources and multipath can be handled well with estimation performances positively correlated with array aperture and the number of snapshots.

articleTitle: Artificial neural network algorithm for predict the photocatalytic activity of the Mn co-doped MgAl2O4: Ce composite photocatalyst
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A gamma-ray irradiation assisted polyacrylamide gel method have been used to synthesize the Mn co-doped MgAl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>: Ce composite photocatalyst. The effects of catalyst load, dye concentration, pH value and irradiation time on the photocatalytic activity of the Mn co-doped MgAl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>: Ce composite photocatalyst were investigated by the degradation of the rhodamine B dye under simulated sunlight irradiation. An artificial neural network model was well-established by using variables including catalyst load, dye concentration, pH value and irradiation time as input layer and degradation rate as output layer. The appropriate neural network model was established to achieve better prediction for the degradation rate and then the response input parameters were used to screen the output data for optimizing the experimental parameters of photocatalytic reaction. The application of presented artificial neural network algorithm can be used as an important tool for predict the photocatalytic activity of the Mn co-doped MgAl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>: Ce composite photocatalyst. This algorithm shows potential applications in material performance prediction, space radiation environment prediction and geological disaster prediction in three gorges reservoir area.

articleTitle: An algorithm using Triple-Frequency Pseudorange-Carrier Phase Combination for Cycle-Slip Detection and Repair
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Cycle-slip detection and repair is indispensable in measurement pre-processing of measuring and monitoring receiver. Based on combination of TurboEdit method and carrier phase, an efficient real-time algorithm using triple-frequency pseudorange and carrier phase is proposed to detect and repair cycle slips in real time. The testing result shows that the method can automatically repair all carrier phase cycle-slips of triple-frequency more than one week, and the consequence is reliable.

articleTitle: A Blanket Jamming Cancelling Algorithm for VHF Radar with Uniform Circular Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to reject blanket jamming for VHF radar based on uniform circular array, a jamming cancelling algorithm with different phase modes are proposed. The zeroth order, the negative first order and the first order phase mode are firstly excited to estimate the azimuth angle of jamming. Then the zeroth order phase mode is used to cancel the jamming in the other two phase modes respectively. At last, the azimuth angle of target can be obtained with the newly constructed phase modes and the azimuth angle of jamming. This algorithm can be applied to suppress various kinds of blanket jamming and its performance depends on the spatial difference between jamming and target. As a supplement, a jamming reconstructing and eliminating method is introduced to deal with the jamming with little amplitude fluctuation such as the noise frequency modulation jamming. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Low-Power RF Signal Detection with High Gain Using a Tunable Optoelectronic Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A novel photonic method for low-power RF signal detection by a tunable optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) based on a dual-parallel Mach-Zehnder modulator (DP-MZM) and a phase-shifted fiber Bragg grating (PS-FBG) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The DP-MZM is utilized to generate the equivalent phase modulation (EPM) signal with partial optical carrier suppression. The EPM is helpful to enhance the gain to the RF signal in the OEO loop. The RF signals from 2 to 18 GHz as low as -87 dBm are detected with a gain of about 10 dB. Compared to normal phase modulation based scheme, the EPM-based system offers 9.1 dB higher gain.

articleTitle: Handwritten Tibetan Digital Words Recognition Based on improved Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper proposes a kind of handwritten Tibetan digital words recognition algorithm, which based on improved convolutional neural network. The algorithm uses the convolution operations and pooling operations to fully extract the features of images. The adaptive learning rate algorithm is applied to the training process of the network, so that the network training rate can improved. Finally, the image features extracted from the neural network are input into the SVM classifier for classification and recognition. The experimental results show that the recognition rate of handwritten Tibetan digital words has been improved significantly. It can be seen that the recognition performance of this algorithm is better than the classic LeNet-5 model.

articleTitle: An Image Formation Algorithm for Cooperative Forward Looking SAR of Manned Aerial Vehicle and UAV with Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Cooperative detection with manned/unmanned aerial vehicles has become a new and promising combat mode with its two-dimensional (2D) and high-resolution imaging advantage of bistatic forward looking. Compared with the traditional synthetic aperture radar (SAR), there exists difference of motion velocity between manned aerial vehicle acted as transmitter and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) acted as receiver in this configuration. In addition, there usually exists acceleration during the UAV movement owing to its rapid response and good maneuverability. Such features result in imaging processing more complicated space-variance property in this special configuration. In this paper, cooperative bistatic forward looking SAR imaging of manned aerial vehicle and UAV with acceleration is studied. A novel phase space-variance correction method for this imaging mode is developed with numerical computation, which effectively improves imaging focus performance on targets.

articleTitle: Malaria Disease Prediction Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Malaria detection is a stressful job for most doctors and it requires experiences and expertise. The machine learing (ML) method can be used to releave this issue. This paper try to find suitable model to help detect malaria with accuracy. The used dataset was released by National Institute of Health in USA and contained a total number of 27,560 red blood cell (RBC) images with equivalent instances of parasitized and uninfected RBCs images. A single hidden layer feedforward neural networks methodology namely Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) model was applied to classify and predict whether a patient has been affected by malaria or not. ELM has been compared with other machine learning techniques like SVM, KNN, CART, RF, CNN, VGG16, RESNET, and DENSENET, and it has outperformed all the other with 99% of accuracy, 28seconds cost time, 0.0095 Misclassification Error, and 98% precision which showed the effectiveness of ELM in the application of malaria cell detection scenario and it can also be referred by other researchers in the related field.

articleTitle: Joint Transmit Beamforming for Multiuser MIMO Communication and MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Nowadays spectrum sharing of radar and communication has becoming a challenging problem. In this paper, we proposed a joint beamforming model for MIMO radar and multiuser MIMO communication sharing spectrum and transmit array. In our model, the transmit array transmits the weighed sums of orthogonal radar waveforms and communication symbols. An optimization problem is formulated to design the weighing coefficients to optimize the performance of MIMO radar transmit beamforming, under the constraints that the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) at each communication user is higher than a given threshold. Although the proposed optimization problem is not convex, we prove that the problem can be converted to a convex one by zero-forcing the inter-user interference. The performance trade-off between radar and communication is shown in the simulation results.

articleTitle: Radar Signal Processing for Low-observable Marine Target-Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sea clutter analysis, suppression, basic and advanced marine target detection and classification techniques, future development are discussed in this paper. Firstly, challenges of marine radar signal processing will be introduced including the challenges of sea clutter suppression, characteristics of complex marine targets, detection and recognition. Subsequently, we will give an overview of popular signal processing techniques from the point of view of detection mechanism, signal modelling, energy integration, radar resolution, and processing domains.
