In view of the above problems, this paper proposes an aircraft target deep learning detection method of lightweight and multi-scale features. On the basis of the multi-scale target detection framework (SSD), the method firstly uses the dense connection structure and the double convolution channels to form the basic backbone networks with feature reuse and high computational efficiency. To improve the detection performance of the small aircraft target, the basis backbone network connects a residual module and deconvolution to compose the multi-scale feature fusion detection module. Compared with the current classical deep learning object detection methods, the experimental results show that the proposed method has the advantages of maintaining low computational complexity and achieving high detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Engineering Calculation Method of Aerodynamic Coefficients for Air-breathing Hypersonic Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper a set of engineering calculation methods based on inviscid flow theory for calculating the aerodynamic forces and moments of a representative air-breathing hypersonic vehicle is presented. The viscosity effect is considered to obtain the drag force more accurately by applying temperature reference method. Unlike conventional aircraft, the experimental data of air-breathing hypersonic vehicles (AHVs) are rare to acquire and the common ways to analyze the aerodynamic characteristics of a new designed AHV are using CFD methods. In this way lots of calculation needs to be done at different points of heights and Mach numbers which will take a relatively long time. Therefore the focus of this paper is on developing a method to calculate aerodynamic forces and moments accurately enough and more rapidly than CFD methods. Simulations results demonstrate that the method has a good performance in calculating the aerodynamic coefficients when applied in the phases of the designing and analyzing the characteristics of AHVs.

articleTitle: A Modified Information Embedding Scheme for the Integrated System of Radar and Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper has proposed a modified information embedding scheme for the integrated system of radar and communication without influence on the mainlobe. Exploiting the waveform diversity of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar, the beamforming weight vectors are designed for constellation mapping to increase the data rate. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Dual DPT for coherent accumulation of high-speed high-maneuvering target
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the development of stealth technology, the high-speed high-maneuvering target is too weak to detect. Traditional fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) and radon Fourier transform (RFT) have good performance in coherent accumulation but need rough estimation of velocity and acceleration in advance. To obtain the rough estimation, a dual discrete polynomial phase transform (DPT) algorithm is proposed in this paper. The DPTs with dual pulse delays are designed and superimposed together to obtain extra signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain. Theoretical derivation and experiment confirm that the output SNR of proposed DPT for high-speed high-maneuvering target has about 2dB gain without reducing the resolution, compared with traditional DPT algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on the optimization strategy of phased array radar multi-area search performance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In most cases, large phased array radars need to search multiple airspace to complete specified tasks. Aiming at the problem that the tracking task occupies the total radar resources and results in the search performance degradation of each airspace, a combined optimization strategy is proposed, which is decomposed into two sub-problems: single-space search parameter adjustment problem and multi-area energy allocation problem. For the first problem, considering the beam broadening effect in the process of scanning and the need for timely adjustment in the search space, a search performance optimization model with the airspace coverage coefficient as the optimization function is established, and three strategies, ASB, AOA and ASBAOA, are given. For the second problem, the weighted airspace coverage coefficient is used as the optimization function to establish the allocation model and two allocation strategies, PAS and AAS, are given. The simulation results show that the performance of ASBAOA and AAS are the best.

articleTitle: Vehicle Tracking in Clutter Environment using High Resolution Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Vehicle tracking using automotive radar is an essential part of autonomous driving. With the resolution of radar increasing, a vehicle generates multiple measurements per time and should be considered as an extended target. By using multiple radar measurements, the tracking algorithm can estimate the kinematic state and extension of vehicle. In this paper, we propose a method to track the vehicle in clutter environment by using extended vehicle model and probabilistic data association with Markov chain Monte Carlo technique. Simulation results show the effectiveness and performance our approach for vehicle tracking under clutter environment.

articleTitle: An Approach for Correction of Ionosphere Phase Contamination Based on Covariance Matrix Recounstruction in Skywave Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: For skywave radar, the radar echo will suffer from phase contamination as they propagate through the time-varying ionosphere, which will lead to serious clutter spectrum spread in long Coherent Processing Interval. It increases the difficulty of the slow-speed target detection and limits the skywave radar performance. In this paper, a decontamination method based on covariance matrix reconstruction is proposed. In this new approach, the stronger one of two Bragg peaks is extracted by an adaptive band-pass filter, then the decontamination function is obtained by the covariance matrix reconstruction. Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that the new scheme is effective and computationally efficient under both slow and fast phase fluctuation.

articleTitle: A new phase unwrapping algorithm combining minimum surface-fitting and network flow for InSAR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Phase unwrapping is a key step of interference synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) signal processing. The unwrapped results can be strongly influenced due to the reason such as noise and under-sampling. The network flow algorithm is able to effectively suppress noise in high coherence regions, as well as overcomes the side effect of `island' phenomenon and confines the error transfer to a very small limit. However, spikes and glitches still exist in the results. Combining the concept of residues, the surface fitting method and the network flow algorithm, this paper proposes a new phase unwrapping algorithm. The new algorithm locates the noise points based on the correlation degree of neighborhood pixels, reconstructs the noise value using minimum surface fitting, and finally corrects the integral results along the integration path. Repeat the iteration until all the noise points are eliminated and many minimum surfaces are fitted repeatedly to form the final unwrapping result. Results obtained from the simulated data and the measured data show that, the proposed method not only achieves better solution with an acceptable time consumption, but also weakens the spikes and glitches as well as restrains the error transfer of the unwrapping process, increasing the precision of phase unwrapping.

articleTitle: Edge-based Differenital Big Data Processing for Sensor-Cloud Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The rise of big data processing and storage bring new challenges for privacy protection. More data, especially personal information, being hosted online such as in cloud, which is out of control. In this paper, we propose an edge-based model for big data processing, taking sensor-cloud data as an example, in which the raw data from wireless sensor networks (WSNs) is differentially processed by algorithms on edge servers. A small quantity of core data is stored on edge and local servers while the rest is transmitted to cloud for storage. In this way, the benefits are twofold. First, the data privacy is preserved since the original data cannot be retrieved even if the data stored in cloud is leaked. Second, implemented by a differential storage method, compared to the state of the art, the edge-based model sends less data to the cloud and reduces the cost of communication and storage. Both theoretical analyses and extensive experiments validate our proposed method.

articleTitle: An Improved Hybrid Freeman/Eigenvalue Decomposition For Polarimetric SAR Data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, the negative power problem in hybrid Freeman/Eigenvalue decomposition is analyzed. To solve this problem, an improved hybrid Freeman/Eigenvalue polarization decomposition method is proposed. Firstly, orientation angle is compensated and phase angle is rotated of coherent matrix through judging dominant scattering mechanism. Secondly, considering the continuous variation of HH and VV ratio, a generalized volume scattering model is introduced into the hybrid decomposition method. Finally, negative power problem in the hybrid Freeman/Eigenvalue decomposition method is further solved by using the nonnegative eigenvalue method. The results are verified by using ESAR data from Oberpfaffenhofen area in Germany. The results show that this method can effectively solve the problem of negative power and the decomposition result is easy to be combined with the actual feature.

articleTitle: Analysis of Effects of Faraday Rotation on Geosynchronous SAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Faraday rotation (FR) is the rotation of the polarization plane relative to the incident wave under the influence of the ionosphere when the signal passes through the ionosphere, which will affect Geosynchronous Synthetic Aperture Radar (GEO SAR) imaging. Due to the long synthetic aperture time characteristic, the time-freezing model assumption for traditional low earth orbit (LEO) SAR imaging will no longer be suitable for GEO SAR imaging analysis. Therefore, the effects of FR on GEO SAR imaging within the extremely long integration time need to be considered. In this paper, the expression of GEO SAR signal under the effects of FR is deduced, and a quantitative analysis for the amplitude-phase error caused by the FR effect in the integration time is conducted. Then, the results of the influence of FR on the amplitude and azimuth phase of the GEO SAR signal are given by using the measured TEC data. Finally, the global distribution map of FR is drawn, and the spatial distribution characteristics of FR are given.

articleTitle: Analysis of Vocal Characteristics of Risso's Dolphins Based on Speech Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Sound is an important method for marine mammal's activity and communication. The sound signals of marine mammals contain a lot of information and theirs character parameters become a key basis for the recognition and protection of marine mammals [1]. In this paper, some features of Risso's dolphin acoustic signals are extracted, includes: duration, pitch frequency and resonance peak etc. A Risso's Dolphin's Acoustic Feature Database was built by these features. By comparing and analyzing the acoustic data of Risso's dolphins, we find that: The frequency domain characteristics of different types of audio signals have some differences, and these differences accord with the corresponding behavioral characteristics of Risso's dolphin.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Conformal Conical Array for Airborne Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Conformal arrays have great potential for providing high performance including wide angle coverage, volume saving and aerodynamic superiority. These potential benefits are attractive for the aircraft that has limited area available for radar installation and requires high radar performance. Conformal conical array is always chosen for its similarity to the aircraft nosecone. The goal of the study is to evaluate the airborne conformal conical array radar performance including anisotropy, beampattern, 3-d cover, power-aperture (PA) product. Numerical results show that the conical array has wider angle coverage and superior performance on PA product than the conventional planar array.

articleTitle: Dual Polarimetric HRRP Sequence Recognition Based on $H/\alpha$ Features
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Dual polarimetric high resolution range prole (HRRP) is able to provide polarimetric and high resolution scattering characteristics information of radar target, which are very useful for automatic target recognition (ATR). In this paper, a novel feature extraction method, which combines both polarimetric and high resolution information, is proposed for dual polarimetric HRRP sequence based on H/α decomposition. In this method, the H/α decomposition is applied on HRRP sequence by temporal average instead of traditional spatial average, which retains the full resolution of HRRP data and provides efficient polarimetric characteristics information of target scattering centers. This paper also presents a scattering mechanisms classification method using the extracted H and α features, and analyzes the effect of noise and clutter on the two features as well as classification performance. The application and effectiveness of the proposed method are demonstrated via outfield experiments. Results show that scattering mechanisms and structural components of a volumetric target are recognized over high resolution range cells, and the proposed method is able to provide support for HRRP sequence-based radar ATR.

articleTitle: No-Reference Defocused Image Quality Assessment Based on Human Visual System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The no-reference image quality assessment is receiving more and more attention. With no need for clear images as a reference during the evaluation process, it has a wide range of application scenarios. By analyzing the characteristics of the defocused image and combining with the Human Visual System (HVS), this paper proposed a No-Reference Visual System Index (NRVSI) approach for the image quality assessment of defoused images. Both the qualitative and quantitative assessments demonstrated the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Formation Design and Accuracy Analysis of GEO-LEO Bistatic InSAR System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The bistatic synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system, based on an inclined geosynchronous earth orbit (GEO) illuminator and a low-earth-orbit (LEO) receiver, has the advantages of high spatial and temporal resolution, higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and good concealment. In this paper, the new system of bistatic InSAR with one GEO transmitter and two LEO receivers is studied. Firstly, we employ Hill equation to design the formation configuration between two LEO SAR receiving platforms. The vertical baseline can be formed between receivers, yielding GEO-LEO bistatic interferometric SAR (InSAR) system. Secondly, under bistatic InSAR interferometric geometry, the positioning equations of InSAR are established, and the elevation measurement accuracy and plane measurement accuracy are analyzed. The simulation results show that the GEO-LEO bistatic InSAR system has good interference performance and can achieve the meter-level interferometric measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: Geometric Correction of Spaceborne SAR Image Based on DEM and ICESat Database
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The accuracy of geolocation is crucial in the application of remote sensing images. However, the presence of inevitable measurement errors consisting of antenna phase center error, slant range error, and reference height error of ground target, will result in degraded the geolocation accuracy of imaged ground targets. To improve the accuracy of geolocation, the approach of geometric correction for spaceborne SAR image is investigated in this paper. The well-known database contained digital elevation model(DEM) and ICESat data are adopted to estimate and calibrate the aforementioned errors for improving the geolocation accuracy. Validation of the proposed method is demonstrated with GF3 SAR data and high-precision GPS device.

articleTitle: Continuous MIMO Radar Waveform Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Current waveform optimization for colocated Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar focuses on pulsed radar. In this paper, we study waveform design for continuous waveform MIMO radar that steers transmit beams toward different directions in a time-division mode. A waveform design criterion is formulated, which tends to fit a given transmit beampattern and to suppress auto/mutual correlation sidelobes of angular waveforms illuminated into different spatial directions. Numerical results are given for transmit beampatterns with one and two peaks to verify the effectiveness of the waveform design criterion. Different from pulsed-radar, angular waveforms associated with continuous-waveform MIMO radar does not bear a bell outline.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Distortion of Sound Echo Reflected by a Cylindrical Object Located in Underwater Multi-path Channel
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper introduces the research work done on distortion of sound echo from a cylinder due to multi-path effect of underwater channel and sound scattering of the object. A sound scattering experiment carried out in water-filled tank is introduced and data processing results are shown and analyzed, which may be useful to research on signal processing of active sonar detection and classification.

articleTitle: GLRT-based persymmetric detectors for wideband radar targets in Gaussian clutter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Adaptive detection of wideband radar targets embedded in homogeneous Gaussian clutter is discussed, by utilizing the persymmetric clutter covariance matrix. Relying on the decision schemes of the one-step and two-step generalized likelihood ratio tests, two adaptive persymmetric detectors are introduced to mitigate the demanding requirement of secondary data. The performance assessment conducted by Monte Carlo simulation confirms their constant false alarm rate properties. And the simulation results furthermore shows that, both aforementioned persymmetric detectors can effectively avoid the collapsing loss resulted from no target scattering in some of the range cells under test.

articleTitle: AsNet: Antenna Selection Learning Network for Mobile Terminal Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output technology is now widely used in mobile devices to improve communication throughput. While additional antenna elements are cheap, RF elements are expensive and lead to high power consumption. Hence, interest is magnified in so-called antenna selection, where only a few out of all antenna elements are chosen. However, most existing antenna selection methods are too complex to be implemented on mobile devices. Industries are encouraged to use the maximum norm method, where the antennas that provide the largest power are selected. In this study, we propose AsNet, an antenna selection technique based on the data-driven deep learning approach. Given large volumes of training data, AsNet can automatically learn to select the best antennas efficiently. Surprisingly, AsNet can achieve similar performance to brute force method and the complexity is only slightly higher than that of random selection.

articleTitle: A Modified S Transform with Adjustable Window Function
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The window function of S transform has a linear relationship with frequency, and it is unable to balance the time resolution of the lower frequency regions with the frequency resolution of the higher frequency regions. A modified S transform is proposed in this paper to overcome the limitations. By establishing an arctangent relationship between frequency and the width of window, the width of the time domain window function can be adaptively changed with frequency within a certain range. This method takes into account the accuracy of time positioning at lower frequencies and the accuracy of frequency positioning at higher frequencies. The simulation results show that the proposed method has better energy aggregation and higher time-frequency resolution.

articleTitle: Supervised Linear Dimensionality Reduction Based on Factor Analysis and Information-Theoertic Criteria
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Recently supervised linear dimensionality reduction method based on Information-Theoretic Criteria has attracted more attention. In existing methods, the first and second order statistics of the data in the original high-dimensional space is estimated, and then the transformation matrix based on the information-theoretic criteria is designed. However, it is difficult to accurately estimate these statistics in the original high-dimensional space, especially in the case of limited data. Thus the transformation matrix obtained may be nonoptimal, which will affect the final classification performance. To solve this problem, a novel supervised linear dimensionality reduction method is proposed in this paper. In our method, the statistical structure of the transformed low-dimensional subspace is described via factor analysis (FA) model, while the mutual information (MI) between the transformed data and their class labels is maximized. Moreover, the joint optimization of MI function and log-likelihood function is achieved, which can not only reduce the estimation errors, but also ensure the separability of the transformed data. Experimental results on benchmark datasets and radar data demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Why Subspace Clustering Works on Compressed Data?
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Subspace clustering (SC) refers to the problem of clustering unlabeled high-dimensional data into a union of low-dimensional subspaces. In many practical scenarios, one may only have access to the compressed data due to constraints of measurement or computation. In this paper, we introduce a general framework for analyzing the performance of various subspace clustering algorithms when applied to the compressed data. Our framework captures the connection between the problems of compressed subspace clustering (CSC) and noisy subspace clustering. With the existing study of noisy SC, our framework makes it possible to easily extend the results in noisy SC to CSC. In this paper, we apply the framework to a most commonly used sparse subspace clustering (SSC) algorithm and obtain its performance. Finally, the practicability and efficiency of CSC are verified by numerical experiments.

articleTitle: DNN-based Speech Enhancement for Improving Speech Quality and Intelligibility Simultaneously
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In many deep learning based speech enhancement frameworks, the deep neural network (DNN) is usually trained under the mean square error (MSE) criterion to estimate the potential clean amplitudes. Yet, the MSE criterion is not directly connected with speech perception, which potentiates alternative training targets for further improvements in speech quality and intelligibility. This paper introduces maximizing the correlation between the enhanced speech and the reference, so as to further improve the speech quality and intelligibility of the enhanced speech synchronously. Based on the short-time Fourier transform amplitude spectra, the correlations are firstly calculated between the envelops along the time and frequency respectively. Then, the time and frequency envelop correlations are incorporated into the time-frequency correlation (TFC). Finally, the loss function is defined as 1 minus the TFC. In experiment, several loss functions containing the time and frequency envelop correlations are investigated. The system trained with the TFC loss outperforms the baseline trained with the MSE loss with promising improvements in both speech quality and intelligibility. Phoneme recognition results also confirm the effectiveness of maximizing the correlation for speech enhancement.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Interference Suppression Capability of MVDR Algorithm Based on Microphone Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: When we experimented on the sound source localization, if the interference and noise in the environment are influential, CBF (Conventional Beam-Forming) algorithms will hardly locate the sound source precisely. In certain situations, the sound source signal could be covered by interference. Consequently, we determine to restrain the effects of noise and interference on sound source localization with the MVDR (Minimum Variance Distortionless Response) algorithm. In the context of a fewer number of array elements and lower snapshots, the MVDR algorithm still sustains loftier resolution. The weight coefficient acquired by the algorithm can minimize the array output power in the anticipant direction. By means of simulation experiments, we broke down the capability of this algorithm including the ability of improving system performance, resolution and interference immunity. Eventually, we use the ICP (Inductively Coupled Plasma) MPA201 microphones and USB-2406 DAQ (Data Acquisition) device to constitute a signal acquisition system to gather the sound source signal. We performed MVDR processing on the factual test data and verified the resolution and interference suppression attribute of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Different Levels Multi-source Remote Sensing Image Fusion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In order to study the fusion methods of multi-source remote sensing image, this paper plans to fuse the optical images and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images in pixel level, feature level and decision level, respectively. For the purpose of combining the merits of fusion at aforementioned levels, the fusion results are assigned different weights for multi-level fusion. Several qualitative and quantitative evaluations are also presented, and they show that the multi-level fusion does pretty-well performance in brightness, sharpness, contrast, amount of information, classification effect, etc. It concludes that the multi-level fusion can significantly extract much information while retaining more details of the original image.

articleTitle: balanced learning-based method for remote sensing aircraft detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Using optical remote sensing image to detect airport aircraft quickly has a wide range of application prospects in many fields. The traditional method based on artificial interpretation has limitations, and has been gradually replaced by the method based on machine learning. With the development of machine learning, convolutional neural network (CNN) has been found to be effective in feature extraction. However, the aircraft target in the optical remote sensing image has some problems, such as the imbalance of samples and the small size of targets. For this reason, we propose a balanced learning for aircraft detection method based on optical remote sensing image, which focuses on the following aspects: (1) A lightweight network is used to improve the detection efficiency. (2) Balanced learning module is implemented to enhance the accuracy. (3) For network learning, a Balanced Orientation method is introduced into our network. Experimental results show that compared with other methods, our method has slightly improved detection performance on the dataset.

articleTitle: A Novel Multiple Hypothesis Tracking Algorithm Integrated with Detection Processing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In current multi-targets tracking system, the multiple hypotheses tracking (MHT) algorithm is considered as the preferred algorithm for data association. However, this method is straightforward, and ignores the couple relationship between detector and tracker, which may result system performance loss. In this paper, we propose a novel multiple hypothesis tracking algorithm integrated with detection processing (MHT-IDP) for multi-target tracking. It explores the idea of integrating the detector with the tracker, in which the tracker guides the detector where to search a target, and the detector provides what is discovered. Moreover, we find that the Bayesian detection threshold is lower near the predicted measurement. Simulation results demonstrate that the MHT-IDP algorithm can improve the clutter suppression effect, enhance the detection performance of the target, and achieve better performance in tracking accuracy compared with the MHT algorithm.

articleTitle: Single-Shot Photonic Time-Stretch Analog-to-Digital Converter Based on Dissipative Soliton
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We demonstrate a photonic time-stretch analog-to-digital converter (ADC) based on dissipative solitons. The dissipative soliton is generated by a passively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser with a net positive group-velocity dispersion in the cavity, which has a large energy spectral density and a relatively flat spectrum with steep edges. The relatively flat spectrum with steep edges can effectively mitigate the signal distortion problem in the time stretch process. The large energy spectral density is favorable for increasing the signal-to-noise ratio of the system. Through employing dissipative solitons in a photonic time-stretch ADC, an effective number of bits of 4.2 bits under an effective sampling rate of 100 GS/s is obtained without adding any optical amplifier in the system.

articleTitle: Rotation-Invariant Fast Template Matching Based on Sequential Monte Carlo
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Template matching is widely applied in Computer Vision. In the case of a template rotation application, it is still nontrivial to find a template matching method with satisfactory matching accuracy and computational complexity. In this work, we propose a fast template matching method based on Sequential Monte Carlo. The method treats the matching process via a Hidden Markov Model(HMM) which establishes a Bayesian framework providing an approximated solution by an importance sampling approach. This solution is utilized to match the template and estimate the position of target template in a background image. Experimental results show a promising template matching improvement in both matching accuracy and matching time.

articleTitle: Efficient Real-time Query of Multimedia Data Based on Local Sensitive Hash
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In recent years, monitoring of modern metropolitan events and civil infrastructure has been identified as an important part of the management of public services. Through rapid information from citizens, intelligent equipment for collecting multimedia information can pass from a terminal initialization, application, examination, provide useful information to deduce such emergency situations. To this end, in this paper, we proposed a realtime query framework in IoT sensing data streams for efficient realtime query of multimedia with hash method. More specifically, the proposed method is featured by: (i) the Batch Orthogonal Locality Sensitive Hashing is adopted to deal with the image and video data with hash code. (ii) a comprehensive flow processing is designed for realtime data query based on storm and kafka. Finally, a series of experiments are presented to evaluate the efficiency and satisfactory performance of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Phase-rotated Spectral Correlation Detector Based Sensing for Wideband Spectrum at Low SNRs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Wideband spectrum sensing plays a key role in cognitive radio. Detecting wideband signals accurately and efficiently at low SNR regimes has recently attracted much interest from the research community. In this paper, two novel wideband sensing methods are presented, sequential sensing using phase-rotated spectral correlation detector (PSCD) and binary sensing using PSCD, which take advantage of PSCD's detection performance at low SNRs. They are explained in detail with diagrams and pseudo codes. Detection performance of the proposed methods in terms of detection probability and false alarm probability are evaluated in additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) environment. The time complexity of the methods is also analyzed. Simulated results indicate that our methods outperform the energy detector at low SNRs.

articleTitle: Signal Correction in UAV Swarm Acoustic Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: UAVs communicate with each other by simple commands using sound, which has the advantages of small interference, autonomous attenuation and proximity interconnection. It can provide emergency support in case of failure of other means of communication such as electromagnetic wave. However, the microphone on the drone acquires a signal from other drones will suffer severe distortion, because of the high-speed motion. That further results in the transmitted signaling information cannot be resolved. In this paper, a distorted signal correction scheme based on generalized S-transform and morphological filtering is proposed to recover the distorted signal. Because the proposed method does not need to know the trajectory of UAV, and does not need to establish geometric model, it has strong practicability. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a simulation case.

articleTitle: Frequency Diversity in Low-Altitude Target DOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In the presence of sea-surface multipath, multipath distortion has been a challenge problem for low elevation target's direction of arrival (DOA) estimation in monopulse radar. Frequency diversity has been explored as a technique in communication to resist multipath and propagation effects. In this paper, approach to integrating frequency diversity into the DOA estimation, that is suitable for sea-surface multipath environment, is proposed. In particular, principles that seek for appropriate frequency selection with higher accuracy of angle measurement, is investigated. Compared with the general circumstances without frequency diversity, the advantage of this method in DOA estimation accuracy for low elevation targets is validated from a theoretical point of view as well as from numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Strong Scatterer Reconstruction Based on Chirp-pulse Microwave Computed Tomography
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The chirp pulse microwave computed tomography (CP-MCT) is an efficient method for weakly scattering objects imaging. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of reconstructing the strong scatterer by adopting the same principle of CT. For this purpose, the chirp pulse is employed to sense an unknown object, thus the delays and attenuations of different paths can be calculated by the Fourier transform, which is known as the microwave time delay spectrum (MTDS). Then, a two-step direct wave extraction method is proposed to pick out the path which interacts with the object straightly. After obtaining the projections at different positions around the object, the TVAL3 algorithm is utilized to reconstruct the scatterer. Finally, numerical simulations validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Accuracy Analysis of Bistatic Active Sonar Ranging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The concealment and anti-interference ability of monostatic sonar system are poor. In-depth theoretical researches and scientific experiments were carried out at home and abroad, meanwhile a lot of meaningful data has been accumulated. In this paper the formulas of ranging and ranging error were given and four factors affecting the error are simulated. The simulation result shows that the sound speed error and time-delay error are the main influence factors of ranging error. The T-R distance error and bearing measurement error can be ignored. The ranging error inducing by time-delay error, T-R distance error and bearing measure error is convergent with increasing distance, but the sound speed error is not convergent with increasing distance.

articleTitle: Robust Wideband Beamforming of Planar Array for Rapidly Moving Interference
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Conventional wideband beamforming methods can only form sharp null in azimuth direction and elevation direction for interference, which will degrade severely in presence of rapidly moving interference. To solve this problem, a robust wideband beamforming method of planar array is proposed. In proposed method, a taper matrix which can broaden the null in azimuth direction and elevation direction is firstly calculated. Then, the array covariance matrix for two dimensional (2D) planar array is reconstructed based on the taper matrix and the sample covariance matrix. Finally, the weight vector of wideband beamforming is calculated based on the constrained least mean-squares algorithm. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Zero-shot Learning with Cross-Layer Neural Network for Emitter Pattern Recognition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The existing emitter pattern recognition methods depend on a large number of labeled samples and are unable to handle unknown samples. Zero-shot Learning (ZSL) can migrate from source classes to target categories by learning a common embedding space, thus realizing the generalization to unknown samples. In this paper, a novel Cross-Layer Neural Network (CLNN) is proposed that integrates different embedding methods into an end-to-end deep learning architecture. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve excellent performances in the presence of unseen radar patterns with either new feature combinations or new feature ranges.

articleTitle: Identification and suppression of clutter using machine learning method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: A clutter suppression method using machine learning method, i.e. random forest, is proposed, which can greatly reduce the false alarm rate in radar target detection. The ground clutter causes great interference to the target detection of the low elevation measurement radar. While the traditional Doppler technology fails to meet the demand of clutter suppression especially in radar measuring small targets with low speed. Polarization information is another important information of the target which is helpful to identify clutter and then to suppress the clutter. The random forest is explored with nine different radar measurement combinations comprising of twelve various polarimetric signatures as input vectors. The results reveal that the random forest can obtain around 93% accuracy when all radar input signatures are used. The application of the method shows that the clutter is well identified and suppressed after filtering.

articleTitle: Simulation of Ship-radiated Noise Based on Shallow Marine Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Ship-radiated noise is the information source for underwater target detection, and it is the basis for sonar and underwater weapons to search and attack the passive targets. In this paper, the hydroacoustic characteristics of ship-radiated noise is studied firstly. Then AR modeling is used to estimate the noise with continuous spectrum, and the sinusoidal signal is used as the model to estimate the noise with line spectrum. Simultaneously, the motion of the ship and the influence of the shallow marine environment are considered as well. Finally, the simulation of the ship-radiated noise is carried out.

articleTitle: A context-aware tracking method for aerial videos
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Remote sensing target tracking in the aerial videos from aerial platforms is one of the research hotspots in visual tracking. In this paper, we propose a remote sensing target tracking method for aerial video based on a context-aware multi-domain convolutional neural network (CAMD). The process can be divided into two main stages: (1) in the design of the tracking network structure, we fuse multiple convolutional layers using residual connections to improve the effectiveness of regression learning. (2) in the “fuzzy interval”, a response-adaptive context-aware correlation filter (RA-CACF) module is introduced into our tracking network to boost the tracking performance. This method can greatly improve both the tracking efficiency and stability. We test the proposed method on the UAV123 datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that our tracker can achieve high accuracy and efficiency results compared to state-of-the-art trackers.

articleTitle: A Computationally Efficient Scheme for FMCW Radar Detection and Parameter Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: This paper presents a computationally efficient scheme for frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar detection and joint angle and frequency estimation in multiple-target scenario. The estimation of the target's parameters is based on the 2D-MUSIC method, and beamspace method is used to reduce the matrix dimension. Lagrangian multiplier method is applied to reduce the quadratic optimization problem in 2D-MUSIC to one-dimensional optimization after beamspace. Digital beam forming (DBF) algorithm is used to increase the probability of targets are detected and provide priori information for beamspace and spectral peak search. Finally, the simulation shows that our system has good performance in target detection ability, resolution ability, estimation accuracy and computational costs.

Index Terms: For Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave Radar

articleTitle: Short-Term Traffic Flow Prediction Based on the Differential Data Graph and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Traffic flow prediction (TFP) is an very important issue for successfully promoting traffic efficiency and reducing traffic congestion in intelligent transportation system (ITS). In this paper, in order to improve the TFP accuracy from the perspective of traffic flow features extraction, we propose a new method named DG-CNN-SVR. The basic thought behind relies on two aspects: the inherit trend in traffic flow data and the some subtle difference at different weekdays. Therefore, we introduce Differential operation to eliminate the trend component and then construct a traffic data Graph to help interpret the complex features. We use convolutional neural network (CNN) for features learning and support vector regression (SVR) for traffic flow predicting. The experimental results by the test data set show that the proposed TFP method performs more effective than the cases when CNN and SVR are used individually.

articleTitle: Research on EIT Image Reconstruction Based on Improved GREIT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is a technique for obtaining internal imaging based on impedance characteristics in the body. Firstly, this paper introduces the basic principles of the back projection algorithm and the Graz consensus Reconstruction algorithm for EIT (GREIT). Then the imaging results of this two algorithms are given by a 2D simulation experiment. Through the comparison of the results, it can be seen that the back projection algorithm has fast imaging speed but the result has obvious radial artifacts, and the GREIT result is better that it has clear edges and realistic shape without artifacts. Meanwhile, the improved GREIT algorithm in this paper eliminates the noise.

articleTitle: Sensor Position Errors Calibration Algorithm of Near-field Source Based on Fourth-order Cumulant
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of array position error calibration under near-field source conditions, a method based on fourth-order cumulant is proposed. Decoupling of azimuth, range and array position error is achieved by vector reconstruction, the rotation invariance of the fourth-order cumulant constructed and transformation of array steering vectors. At the same time, the position error is calibrated in a time-sharing manner by using multiple signal sources at different positions. But this method does not require a precisely known auxiliary source. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has less computational complexity, more accurate azimuth and range parameters estimation, and higher accuracy of position error calibration.

articleTitle: Underwater Target Recognition Method Based on Convolution Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the underwater target radiated noise recognition under the limitation of low signal-to-noise ratio and small number of labeled samples, the deep learning method of convolutional autoencoder is proposed for target noise time-frequency image recognition. According to the characteristics of underwater acoustic target noise, the convolutional autoencoder models with different number of convolution layers were constructed. Then, the unsupervised training based on noisy samples without labels and supervised tuning based on labeled samples were implemented for the models in sequence. The experimental data processing results show that the unsupervised training can effectively purify data noise and improve the separability of dimensionality reduction features to a certain extent. And after supervised training, the separability of features can be greatly improved. At the same time, the recognition accuracies of convolutional autoencoder models are better than that of the contrast methods, which verifies its effectiveness for underwater target recognition.

articleTitle: The W-disjoint Orthogonality of Underwater Acoustic Signals and Underdetermined Source Counting for Acoustic Vector Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we survey the multi-sources distinguish ability of the direction of arrival (DOA) histogram based on acoustic vector sensor (AVS) by verifying the W-disjoint orthogonality (WDO) of the underwater acoustic signals. The relationships between the WDO property and the source number, frequency and window length were studied. We also conduct the underdetermined source counting by modeling the DOA histogram from AVS as a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) with a Dirichlet prior. The parameters of the GMM are estimated by a maximum a posteriori (MAP) approach employing the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm. The underdetermined sources are counted by picking out the Gaussian components fitting to the source clusters according to the estimated parameters.

articleTitle: Distributed Radar Robust Location Error Calibration Based on Interplatform Ranging Information
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Distributed radar system has many working modes, such as target search and detection, receiving coherence, transmitting coherence and SAR imaging, so it has important research value. The realization of the above modes depends on the accurate positioning of radar nodes themselves, that is, spatial synchronization. However, when a distributed radar system is in a dense building area, the satellite-based time/space/frequency (phase) synchronization performance will be weakened due to the reduction of the number of satellites visible at the same time. Therefore, it is necessary to correct spatial synchronization errors based on radar echo data in distributed radar scenarios with time/space/frequency (phase) synchronization errors. In this paper, a robust spatial synchronization correction technique for distributed radar system is completed based on inter-platform ranging information. Firstly, a target echo model of distributed radar with synchronization error is established, and the influence of positioning error on distributed radar system is analyzed. Then, a robust spatial synchronization calibration technique for distributed radar system is proposed, and an achievable hardware scheme is constructed. Finally, the validity of the proposed scheme is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Majorization Minimization based Memetic Algorithm for Designing Polyphase Sequences with Good Correlation Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Polyphase sequences with low aperiodic autocorrelation sidelobes are well known to have extensive applications in communication and radar systems. In this paper, we present an effective algorithm named Majorization Minimization based Memetic Algorithm (MA-MM) to design such sequences. Compared with the previously proposed algorithms, this algorithm searches the solution space more efficiently to obtain a global solution with much better autocorrelation properties. It can be used to minimize the integrated sidelobe level (ISL) and peak sidelobe level (PSL), respectively. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms. It is demonstrated that the proposed algorithms can generate sequences with much better autocorrelation properties compared with some well-known analytical sequences. In addition, the influence of some parameters on the performance of the designed sequences is investigated.

articleTitle: A Real-time Visual UAV Detection Algorithm on Jetson TX2
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are now widely used in civil applications. Uncontrolled UAVs may cause some harm to the order of flight fields and other places. An adaptive UAV detection algorithm based on maximally stable extremal regions method is proposed for small target detection of UAV in video. By optimizing the MSER algorithm, this UAV detection algorithm can detect video in real time and has sufficient robustness. At the same time, we combined discriminative scale space tracker algorithm to test the existing video, and got good real-time performance. Considering the practical application scenarios, we use NVIDIA Jetson TX2 to test the algorithm and collate the results. The results show that our method performs well.

articleTitle: Mainlobe Jamming Suppression with Frequency Diverse Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The range-angle beam-pattern of frequency diverse array has the potential to deal with main-lobe jamming. Regardless of the beam-pattern's time-variance, the transmit-receive beam-pattern can focus on targets in range and angle dimensions. But the range-angle beam-pattern of FDA cannot distinguish between the true targets and the false targets generated by the jammer. The received false targets' signal is in the same with the true targets' in the same place. In order to suppress the main-lobe jamming, a novel transmitting beampattern synthesis method of FDA is proposed to solve mainlobe jamming.

articleTitle: A maneuvering tracking method based on LSTM and CS model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Maneuvering target tracking is an important research field in radar tracking. In recent years, the development of machine learning provides a new idea for maneuvering target tracking. This paper presents a trajectory recognition method based on LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) and a maneuvering tracking method using matched CS (current statistics) model parameter. This method makes use of the characteristics of LSTM that can effectively combine the above information to realize the recognition of target motion states. Then, clustering analysis is used to obtain the optimal filtering parameters of each motion mode in the statistical sense, and filtering is carried out according to the recognition results of LSTM. Compared with the traditional maneuvering tracking method, this method can maintain stable filtering gain in the duration of maneuvering, and the filtering accuracy is improved.

articleTitle: Real-time Remote Sensing Video Compression for On-orbit Heterogeneous Platform
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of optical remote sensing (RS) satellites, RS video has replaced RS image as the main way to obtain information in orbit environment. However, the storage and transmission of on-orbit RS video faces enormous challenges: the contradiction between limited power, space and bandwidth and massive video data volume is becoming increasingly acute. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an effective implementation of spaceborne real-time RS video compression based on CPU+GPU heterogeneous framework. First, we propose a new rate control method based on HEVC for on-orbit RS video compression, which allocates less bitrate for low complexity code blocks (CBs) and more bitrate for high complexity CBs, which can improve the accuracy of rate control algorithm while ensuring compression quality. Then this paper makes full use of the CPU + GPU heterogeneous framework to speed up the whole compression processing. The experimental results show that the proposed compression framework realizes 200x real-time compression of 1080p spaceborne RS video with a PSNR greater than 38.7 dB.

articleTitle: Moving target detection based on Circular Video SAR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Video Synthetic Aperture Radar (Video-SAR) achieves radar video observation by continuously monitoring a certain area to form continuous image data of the target, and it plays an important role in civil and military fields. The SAR image of the moving target is defocused and deviates from its true position, but in its real position, a shadow area similar to the target size is generated. In this paper, the shadow area is used to detect the moving target. Firstly, the image sequence is de-noised by wavelet analysis. Then the maximum threshold segmentation of Tsallis gray entropy is performed. The SIFT and FAST algorithms are used to detect and match the corners of each frame. At the same time, the RANSAC algorithm is used to optimize the pairing results to complete the image registration. Finally, the moving target is extracted by the three-frame difference method, and the result is marked to the corresponding position of the original image. Based on the Video SAR segment published by Sandia Labs in the United States, the detection of the largest moving vehicle in the video is realized, and the effectiveness and anti-interference of the proposed algorithm is verified.

articleTitle: Adaptive Joint Channel Estimation of Digital Self-Interference Cancelation in Co-time Co-frequency Full-Duplex Underwater Acoustic Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: We propose a new channel estimation technology of digital self-interference cancellation method to solve the severe self-interference problem of co-time co-frequency full-duplex communication in underwater acoustic communication. Generally, the intended signal is regarded as interference during the self-interference channel estimation. In this paper, self-interference signal and intended signal are combined based on adaptive algorithm to estimate self-interference and intended channel. We use the self-interference channel obtained by the proposed method to reconstruct self-interference signal for digital self-interference cancellation. Compared with the self-interference channel method that use only self-interference signal, our proposed method has higher accuracy, improves the performance of digital self-interference cancellation, and improves the performance of Co-time Co-frequency full-duplex underwater acoustic communication.

articleTitle: Human Target Enhancement Based on Radon Fourier Transform in Through-Wall Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Through-wall imaging radar (TWIR) usually transmits ultra-wideband (UWB) signals to obtain high-range resolution and penetrate walls to image the concealed human targets. Because of the round-trip high attenuation of walls and low reflectivity of human target, the received human target echoes are extremely weak, and consequently it is necessary to enhance the human target echoes and improve the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) before image formation. However, directly applying the conventional moving target detection (MTD) is faced with the range migration issue due to the high-range resolution of UWB TWIR. In this paper, we introduce the radon-Fourier transform (RFT) into the UWB TWIR to enhance the human target echo in the velocity domain, which can overcome the range migration. Simulation results show that noise can be effectively suppressed and target echoes can be significantly enhanced.

articleTitle: Discrete Dynamic Bayesian Network Threat Assessment Method Based on Cloud Parameter Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the data is easily divided inaccurately at the conceptual junction after the discretization of the target continuous threat variable, a Discretization Dynamic Bayesian Network (DDBN)parameter learning algorithm based on cloud model is proposed. The cloud model is adopted to realize softening points from continuous quantitative data to qualitative concepts, to obtain the soft probability that the data belongs to the qualitative concept; On this basis, the state concept is expanded and replicated in proportion to probability, and multiple sets of hard evidence samples are obtained, and then the parameter learning is performed; the learned parameters are used for threat reasoning, and the posterior probability that the target belongs to each threat level is obtained. Threat ranking is carried out by introducing utility theory and the simulation results verify the rationality of the target threat assessment under the condition of the small sample data missing.

articleTitle: A Closed-Form Solution for Moving Target Localization in Distributed MIMO Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: An algebraic closed-form two-stage weighted least square method with auxiliary variables for locating a moving target using time delay and Doppler shift in distributed multiple-input multiple-output radar systems is proposed in this paper. In the first stage, a set of linear equations about target position and velocity is established firstly, and then a closed-form weighted least square (WLS) method is adopted to achieve the estimate. In the second stage, new linear equations with auxiliary variables are created, and then another closed-form WLS solution is derived. The final estimate is demonstrated, by both theory and simulations, to be approximately unbiased, and its covariance is equal to the Cramer-Rao lower bound under small noise conditions. According to the simulation results, the localization performance of the proposed method is better than that of the state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on the Key- frame Extraction of Surveillance Video Based on Motion Velocity
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: People pay more attention to the change of object motion in surveillance video. Therefore, this paper proposes a key frame extraction method based on motion velocity. This method firstly extracts the moving object, next calculates the velocity of object and processes the velocity, then generates the motion velocity curve of the object, and finally extracts the key frames of the surveillance video according to the curve. Experimental results reveal that the proposed method can accurately extract the video frames whose motion changes in the process of object motion.

articleTitle: Range-Angle Decoupled Estimation based on Grouped Frequency Coding Method in Monostatic FDA-MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, a grouped frequency coding strategy is proposed for joint range-angle estimation in monostatic FDA-MIMO radar system. Different from traditional phased array radar, frequency diversity array radar has angle-dependent and range-dependent beampattern. The resulting coupling phenomenon from a single frequency increment of transmitting signal makes it impossible to locate targets accurately. This phenomenon can be avoided by adding other frequency groups with different increments codes. However, the periodic repetition of estimation usually results in false peaks. In order to eliminate false targets and further increase the resolution, the additional searching codes in preorder and screening codes in postorder are designed. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Efficient and Lightweight Target Recognition for High Resolution Spaceborne SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Fast and reliable target recognition of the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images has been widely used in the fields of the marine monitoring, military reconnaissance and strike all over the world. However, due to the difficulty of the intra-class difference and inter-class similarity of the multiclass targets in the high resolution SAR images, the existing methods are difficult to recognize the targets accurately when facing the spaceborne platforms with the high resource constraints. Therefore, in order to solve the above problems, we propose a novel recognition method based on the convolutional neural network (CNN). Firstly, we propose a lightweight CNN framework which regards densely connected convolutional network (DenseNet) as the baseline. Secondly, we advocate a strong discriminative loss function which efficiently improves the recognition accuracy of the targets in the spaceborne SAR images. Experiments are conducted on the TerraSAR dataset and MSTAR dataset to evaluate the proposed method. The results show that our method performs better than the baseline on the both benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: An Image Segmentation Method for the blind sidewalks recognition by using the convolutional neural network U-net
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The image segmentation for the blind sidewalks recognition is important for the blind guide system, which can help the visually impaired people to go out freely. In the paper, we have proposed an image segmentation method for blind sidewalks recognition by using the convolutional neural network (CNN) U-Net. It is theoretically analyzed and numerically proved that the blind sidewalk region can be effectively segmented without requiring a large number of the labeled training samples by using the proposed method. And the mean value for the dice similarity coefficient (DSC) is more than 90% in the proposed method. Besides, the running time for random image segmentation is less than 0.5 second, which can easily satisfy the request for real-time image recognition.

articleTitle: Small ship detection in SAR images based on modified SSD
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Small object detection is a nodus for CNNs (Convolutional Neural Networks) that take advantages of feature pyramid for object detection, and it is also a hotspot which researchers focus on, especially small ship detection in SAR images. Based on SSD (Single Shot Multibox Detector), which is a classical CNN detector and a typical one-stage method for object detection, and inspired by the ideas of object enhancement and feature fusion, the paper uses deconvolution to enhance representation of small object in feature pyramid. Thereby we expect to improve detecting precision of SSD. The feasibility and effectiveness of proposed method are proved by our experiments. Experimental results on SSDD show that the proposed method greatly improves detecting precision of small ships in SAR images.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Different Approaches of Convolutional Neural Networks for Land Use and Land Cover Classification Based on High Resolution Remote Sensing Images
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Land use and land cover mapping is very important in the fields of urban planning, land management, and natural resource conservation. Recently, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are applied widely in land use and land cover (LULC) classification as the acquisition of high resolution satellite images becomes easier owing to technological advancements. In this paper, we explore how to better exploit existed CNNs in LULC classification task. Three different learning modalities: full-trained, fine-tuning and pre-trained CNNs were used as feature extractors, and two promising CNNs models (AlexNet and GoogLeNet) and two remote sensing datasets (UC Merced Land Use dataset and Brazilian Coffee Scenes dataset) were studied. Results show that the both AlexNet and GoogLeNet can be used in high remote sensing classification with a great performance. What is more, the full-trained CNNs is not always the best approach, on the contrary, fine-tuning based on pre-trained CNNs, tends to be the best approach.

Index Terms: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge
Author Keywords: land use and land cover classification

articleTitle: Optical Remote Sensing Images Feature Extraction of Forest Regions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: The forest region saliency extraction technology based on optical remote sensing image plays an important role in forest fire risk monitoring and forest area protection in the process of urbanization. In this paper, the large-area forest area in the optical remote sensing image is highlighted in the feature map, and the salient map is further obtained through the generated feature map to achieve accurate extraction of the optical remote sensing image forest area. Feature extraction includes two parts: adaptive color region extraction through DC (Definition Circle Model) model and corner feature extraction including suppression mechanism through edge detection model. After a series of experiments, the feature-significant extraction technique is more adaptive and accurate than other unsupervised target detection models.

articleTitle: Multi-target Localization with MIMO Radar via Coupled Canonical Polyadic Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, we innovatively introduce coupled canonical polyadic decomposition (C-CPD) into a Multi-Static-Multi-Pulse MIMO radar system, which consists of one transmit subarrays and multiple spatially-distributed receive subarrays, to localize targets. In the system, the received signals at each receive array can be stacked into a third-order tensor that admits CPD, and these tensors together follow C-CPD. Therefore C-CPD based algorithms can be applied to these stacked tensors to calculate the related factor matrices, some of which can be used to extract the position information of the targets, as presented in this paper. It is worth noting that our used method does not require the probing signals are mutually orthogonal. Nor do their waveforms need to be known. Experimental results shown in the last section will validate all of our claims.

articleTitle: Target Geometric Configuration Estimation Based on Acoustic Scattering Spatiotemporal Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Target geometric configuration estimation is an important field in underwater target recognition. In this paper, the estimation of underwater target geometric configuration is studied combined with the joint characteristics in time domain and space domain of high frequency acoustic scattering. Firstly, the omni-directional acoustic scattering model of target in near field at high frequency is established, and the estimation method of scattering highlights is proposed by high resolution DOA estimation, time delay compensation and data fusion technique. The geometric configuration of the Benchmark submarine model is estimated by computer simulation. The simulation result shows that the estimated result of the target geometric configuration is consistent with the actual value of the target, which verified the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Network Connectivity Performance Analysis of Platoon-based Vehicular Ad-hoc Network on a Two-Way Lane
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Vehicular ad-hoc network (VANET) is an Ad-hoc network with fast dynamic characteristics. Achieving reliable end-to-end communications in VANET is changeling due to the fast moving of vehicles. To this end, network connectivity has become an important performance indicator for VANET quality and it is necessary to enhance the network connectivity to transfer information more efficiently and quickly. In this paper, the connectivity probability is mainly analyzed for Vehicle-to-Infrastructure(V2I) communications. In order to make the research more close to the real fact, we study the connectivity characteristic of platoon-based VANET on a two-way lane. Some key parameters are also investigated in order to analyze the impact connectivity performance, including the vehicle speed, the distance between BS, the vehicle arrival rate, the vehicle communication range, the ratio of vehicles transmit signals and the vehicle safety distance, respectively. The simulation shows that the network connectivity probability of platoon-based VANETs on a two-way lane is significantly higher than those on a one-way Lane or without platoons.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Environmental Sound Classification Based On Topological Persistence
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Environmental sound classification (ESC) is a significant problem in signal processing and machine learning. In this paper, a novel unsupervised learning approach is proposed using topological data analysis. Each sound signal is transformed into a point cloud by time-delay embedding. The persistence diagrams are obtained after computing the persistent homology of Vietoris-Rips filtrations. The sound signals are assigned to different classes using kmeans algorithm based on the bottleneck distance matrix of persistence diagrams.

articleTitle: An Improved Harmonic Suppression Method Based on Adaptive Compensation Algorithm for Monobit Receiver
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Monobit receiver is widely used in electronic warfare due to its large instantaneous receiving bandwidth, high sensitivity and high dynamic range. However, in the procedure of signal processing, monobit receiver generates high harmonics because of nonlinear quantization operations. These harmonics greatly reduce the instantaneous dynamic range (IDR) of the simultaneous signal, thereby reducing the performance of the monobit receiver. Meanwhile, the existing suppression methods are of great storage space and computational complexity. Aiming at the disadvantages in suppression efficiency, storage space, computational complexity and the balance between them of existing harmonic suppression methods, this paper proposes an improved harmonics suppression method based on adaptive compensation algorithm (ACA). Firstly, the peak frequency of signal spectrum is detected by monobit DFT, and the positions of the harmonics are located according to the peak frequency. Secondly, the sidelobe-to-maximum adjacent unit ratio (SMR) criterion is proposed, and each harmonic in compensation vector from the pre-stored compensation matrix is evaluated whether it needs to be compensated according to this criterion. Then, the adaptive compensation vector of each harmonic is used to suppress the harmonic components in the signal spectrum selectively. Finally, Updating the signal spectrum and performing the simultaneous signal detection based on proportional threshold. The simulation results show that the proposed method effectively suppresses the harmonics under different signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) when compared to the traditional compensation algorithm and its improved algorithms. Meanwhile, the proposed method greatly improves IDR with less computational complexity and is easier to implement in engineering.

articleTitle: Shot Boundary Detection Based on HSV Color Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: In this paper, the traditional algorithm of shot boundary detection based on histogram difference is introduced briefly. Based on this, a video shot boundary detection algorithm based on HSV color model is proposed. The method firstly detects the shot hard cut based on the weighted color histogram difference curve, then performs the shot gradual transition detection according to the image local average pixel value characteristic curve. Finally, two partial detection results are fused, and all the shot transitions of the video can be obtained. Experimental result shows that the method has a higher recall and precision.

articleTitle: A 3D Reconstruction Method of Mountain Areas for TomoSAR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Tomographic Synthetic Aperture Radar (TomoSAR) is an advanced technique which allows to achieve 3D reconstruction of interested areas, such as man-made buildings, mountain areas, and other topographic features. However, up to now there exist few researches about 3D reconstruction of mountain areas using TomoSAR. In this paper, an efficient 3D reconstruction method of mountain areas for TomoSAR is proposed. It is a point cloud postprocessing method, which exploits secondary denoising and local plane fitting in a projected coordinate system. Compared with traditional algorithms, the proposed method can not only obtain a good denoising performance, but also acquire high quality 3D reconstruction images of mountain areas. The effectiveness of our method is verified by both simulated and experimental results.

articleTitle: The Processing of synchronous double pulse laser induced acoustic signal
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Signal, Information and Data Processing (ICSIDP)
abstract: Based on theoretical analysis and high-speed camera measurement experiment, this paper investigated the following subjects: laser-generated cavitation phenomenon and the interaction between two laser-generated bubbles.
